[the optimization model](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../explanation/optimization-model.html.md) for why plain SAT
feasibility is not enough here.

# Without root_priority: list order decides

```json
{
  "toolchain": {"name": "foss", "version": "2025b"},
  "roots": ["GROMACS", "LAMMPS"],
  "pins": [],
  "forbid": [],
  "objective": "prefer_newer"
}
```

With no `root_priority` field, priority defaults to `roots` list order:
listing `GROMACS` first here keeps `GROMACS 2025.0` (and `OpenMPI 4.1.6`),
yielding `LAMMPS 2023.08`. Reordering `roots` to `["LAMMPS", "GROMACS"]`
flips the outcome to `LAMMPS 2024.08` / `GROMACS 2024.4`. That coupling
(priority tied to incidental list order) is exactly what `root_priority`
lets you avoid.

# With root_priority: explicit and list-order-independent

```json
{
  "toolchain": {"name": "foss", "version": "2025b"},
  "roots": ["LAMMPS", "GROMACS"],
  "root_priority": ["GROMACS", "LAMMPS"],
  "pins": [],
  "forbid": [],
  "objective": "prefer_newer"
}
```

```bash
eb-stack stack solve \
  --easyconfigs fixtures/two_root_openmpi_conflict/easyconfigs \
  --stack-policy fixtures/two_root_openmpi_conflict/policies/priority_gromacs_roots_lammps_first.json \
  --lock-out /tmp/root-priority.lock.json --sbom-out /tmp/root-priority.cdx.json
# GROMACS 2025.0 (kept: prioritized)
# LAMMPS 2023.08 (yielded: not prioritized)
# OpenMPI 4.1.6 (forced by GROMACS's exact pin)
```

`roots` still lists `LAMMPS` first, but ~root_priority: ["GROMACS",
"LAMMPS"]` keeps `GROMACS~ at its newest version regardless. Swap the
`roots` order in the policy file and re-run: the outcome does not change,
because priority is now declared, not inferred.

# How the priority is applied

For each root in `root_priority` order (or `roots` order when
`root_priority` is omitted), `eb-stack` pins that root to the newest version
that is **still jointly feasible** with every higher-priority root already
pinned, then moves to the next root. Lower-priority roots yield whatever
version remains consistent once the higher-priority pins are fixed. A root
missing from an explicit `root_priority` list is appended in `roots` order,
so every root always participates.

# Next steps

- [Policy schema reference](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../reference/policy.html.md) for the exact
  `root_priority` field semantics.
- [[file:../explanation/optimization-model.org][Why this needs an optimization layer
  on top of SAT feasibility]].

# Which easyconfigs an easyblock change reaches

A change to an easyblock, generic or software-specific, or to a framework
module an easyblock imports, reaches the easyconfigs that use that class.
The class may be the `easyblock` line, the implied `EB_<Name>` class, a
subclass, an extension class, or a bundle component class.

# One changed file

`scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh` creates a checkout of the pinned trees and writes
`env.sh`. `EB_EASYBLOCKS` is easybuild-easyblocks v5.4.1.
`EB_EASYCONFIGS` is the develop easyconfigs directory.
`EB_EASYBUILD_FRAMEWORK` is easybuild-framework v5.4.1. Source `env.sh`
and pass those paths.

```bash
scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh
set -a
source "${EB_UPSTREAM_CACHE:-$HOME/.cache/eb-stack/upstream}/env.sh"
set +a
printf '%s\n' 'CMake/4.2.1-GCCcore-15.2.0' > /tmp/modules.txt

eb-stack easyblock-reach \
  --easyblocks "$EB_EASYBLOCKS" \
  --easyconfigs "$EB_EASYCONFIGS" \
  --file "$EB_EASYBLOCKS/easybuild/easyblocks/generic/cmakemake.py" \
  --installed /tmp/modules.txt \
  --reverse \
  --out-dir /tmp/cmakemake-reach
```

That command, against the trees `scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh` checked
out on 2026-10-24, printed:

```
easyconfigs=2352 installed=0 classes=39 reverse=5058 out=/tmp/cmakemake-reach
```

`installed` stays 0 when the modules file does not name a reached
module. The empty range `HEAD..HEAD` on that same checkout printed
`easyconfigs`0 installed`0 classes`0 reverse`0`.

`modules.txt` lists installed modules, one per line:
`name/version[-toolchain]versionsuffix`. Blank lines and `#` comments are
ignored.

The command writes `reach.toml`, `reach.json`, and `reach.md`. The TOML
file starts with the generated-file header. The markdown opens with the
same warning as an HTML comment. Neither is a file to merge.

# A commit range or a pull request

```bash
eb-stack easyblock-reach \
  --easyblocks "$EB_EASYBLOCKS" \
  --easyconfigs "$EB_EASYCONFIGS" \
  --range HEAD..HEAD \
  --out-dir /tmp/range-reach

eb-stack easyblock-reach \
  --easyblocks "$EB_EASYBLOCKS" \
  --framework "$EB_EASYBUILD_FRAMEWORK" \
  --easyconfigs "$EB_EASYCONFIGS" \
  --pr 4250 \
  --repo "$EB_EASYBLOCKS" \
  --base easybuild-easyblocks-v5.4.1 \
  --out-dir /tmp/pr4250-reach
```

`--range` is passed to `git diff --name-only`. `HEAD..HEAD` on the
pinned checkout changes no file. `--pr` fetches `refs/pull/N/head` and
diffs it against the merge-base with `--base` (default `develop`). The
pinned easyblocks checkout is the v5.4.1 tag, so pass
`--base easybuild-easyblocks-v5.4.1` when that is the tree `--repo`
has. `--repo` is the clone `git` reads; it defaults to the first
`--easyblocks` path. The class hierarchy is the working tree. A
deleted file is read from the base so its class is still seen.

# What counts as a use

- the `easyblock` line
- no `easyblock` line: `EB_<Name>` derived from the software name
- a subclass, read from the Python `class` statement, so `EB_GROMACS(CMakeMake)`
  is reached by a change to `CMakeMake`
- a nested class, so `EB_QuantumESPRESSOcmake(CMakeMake)` inside
  `EB_QuantumESPRESSO` reaches the QuantumESPRESSO easyconfigs
- a module-level alias bound to a class, so `Legacy = CMakeMake` is
  `CMakeMake`
- an extension's own `easyblock`, else `EB_<extname>` when that class
  exists, else `exts_classmap`, else `exts_defaultclass`
- a component's own `easyblock`, else `EB_<name>` when that class exists,
  else `default_easyblock`

A class that assigns `exts_defaultclass` overwrites the easyconfig.
`PythonBundle` assigns `PythonPackage`, including from inside `with`.
For a component, `default_easyblock` in the easyconfig wins over the
class.

A framework module reaches the easyblocks that import it, then their
subclasses. Imports inside `easybuild.framework` and `easybuild.tools`
are followed to the end of that graph. An easyblock that imports any
module on that path is reached. An easyblock that only imports another
easyblock is not, unless it subclasses a reached class.

`--reverse` lists modules that depend on a reached module and would need a
rebuild: runtime, builddependency, extension, or toolchain. Reached modules
are not listed again.

# Find shared builds across open pull requests

Two open pull requests on the European Environment for Scientific
Software Installations (EESSI) software-layer often build the same
dependency. If both are merged and built, the second build overwrites
the first. `eb-stack pr-overlap` lists the modules each open pull
request (PR) would still build, which of those modules more than one
PR would build, and, with `--merge-order`, an order that builds each
shared module once.

Use it before you merge a batch of open software-layer PRs that share
a dependency. The command analyzes easyconfig and easystack text and
writes report files. It does not run EasyBuild or modify a pull
request.

# Run the recorded fixture

This repository records two software-layer PRs under
`tests/pr_overlap_layer`. Run this from the repository root:

```bash
eb-stack pr-overlap --pr tests/pr_overlap_layer/prs.json \
  --easyconfigs tests/pr_overlap_layer \
  --installed tests/pr_overlap_layer/installed.txt \
  --installed-label none \
  --generated-at 2026-10-24T00:00:00Z \
  --repo-url https://github.com/EESSI/software-layer \
  --eessi-version 2026.06 \
  --merge-order \
  --out-dir /tmp/pr-overlap-out
```

The command prints:

```
prs=2 records=2 shared_modules=91 skipped_easyconfigs=0 out=/tmp/pr-overlap-out
```

`prs` is how many pull requests were read. `records` is how many of
them add at least one entry to an easystack for this version. A pull
request with no such entry stays in `prs` and stays out of `records`.
Each record has a `to_build` list, the build set: the modules that PR
would still build. `shared_modules` counts modules in more than one
build set. `skipped_easyconfigs` is how many recipe files the parser
could not parse. `out` is the directory containing `overlap.md`,
`overlap.toml`, one `prs/<N>.toml` file per record, and, with
`--merge-order`, `merge-order.toml`.

Pull request 1585 adds `SciPy-bundle/2026.05-gfbf-2026.1`. Pull
request 1728 adds `PLUMED/2.10.0-foss-2026.1`, and that recipe depends
on SciPy-bundle 2026.05. The fixture's `installed.txt` is a single
comment line, so nothing counts as already built. The fixture is a
replay: both PRs have since merged, and the titles in the report are
the merge-commit subjects stored in `prs.json`. Both PRs are run
against an empty installed list, which is why they share 91 modules,
including compilers such as `GCC/15.2.0`.

# Read the report

The top of `overlap.md` from this run is:

```text
<!-- Generated by `eb-stack pr-overlap`. This branch is never merged. -->
# Shared builds between open pull requests (2026.06)

Computed 2026-10-24T00:00:00Z against the modules installed for `none`. 2 pull requests change an easystack for this version.

## Modules more than one pull request would build

| Module | Pull requests |
|---|---|
```

The line under the title names the installed list (`none` here). The
table has one row per shared module, 91 rows in this run. SciPy-bundle
is one of them:

```text
| `SciPy-bundle/2026.05-gfbf-2026.1` | [#1585](https://github.com/EESSI/software-layer/pull/1585), [#1728](https://github.com/EESSI/software-layer/pull/1728) |
```

Read that row as: both pull requests would build this module, so one
build has to finish before the other starts. Further down, the section
for pull request 1585 gives a build count of 91 modules, and the
section for pull request 1728 gives 109. All 91 of 1585's modules are in
1728's build set.

`--merge-order` also writes `merge-order.toml`. These lines are from
that file. Each step's `builds` line, and the `modules` list under
`steps.saves`, is one long line of module names and is left out here.

```text
[[steps]]
position = 1
pr = 1585
after = []
reason = "smallest residual build set (91)"

[[steps.saves]]
pr = 1728

[[steps]]
position = 2
pr = 1728
after = [1585]
saves = []
reason = "smallest residual build set (18)"
```

Merge in `position` order. `after` lists the PRs that must merge
first. Pull request 1728 must wait for pull request 1585, because
1585 adds SciPy-bundle to the easystack by name, while 1728 only
reaches it as a dependency of PLUMED. When two or more PRs are free to go
next, the one with the fewest modules left to build goes first, and
`reason` records that count. The word "residual" in `reason` means
those modules left to build. In step 1, no earlier PR is required,
and pull request 1585 has 91 modules left to build. The
`[[steps.saves]]` entry says that building those modules for 1585
removes the same 91 modules from 1728's later build. In step 2, pull
request 1728 has `after = [1585]`, and 18 modules remain, including
PLUMED.

The same order is the Merge order table at the end of `overlap.md`.
Merge and build pull request 1585 first, and pull request 1728 second.

`prs/<N>.toml` is that PR's build set. `overlap.toml` is the same
shared-module index as data. Field names are in
[output formats](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../reference/formats.html.md). A PR omitted from
the current input has no file: each run rewrites `prs/` to contain
only records from that run. The live fetch supplies open PRs; static
`--pr` files are not checked for open or closed status. How one
easystack line becomes a build set, and how that order is chosen, is in
[from one easystack line to a build set](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../explanation/pr-overlap.html.md).

# Run it on a mounted stack

You need three things: the EESSI repository mounted under
`/cvmfs/software.eessi.io`, a clone of `EESSI/software-layer` as the
working directory, and a logged-in `gh`. The CPU target in this example is
`x86_64/amd/zen4`. Source the EESSI init script and load the extend
module before the block below:

: source /cvmfs/software.eessi.io/versions/2026.06/init/lmod/bash
: module load EESSI-extend

That sets `EESSI_SOFTWARE_PATH` (the install prefix for the CPU target
you loaded) and `EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS`. Set `EB_STACK_CHECKOUT` to an
eb-stack checkout. Set `EB_EASYCONFIGS` and `EB_EASYBLOCKS` to the
easyconfig tree and the `easybuild/easyblocks` package for the
EasyBuild version these easystacks name.
`scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh` clones a pinned release, which can
differ from that version.
`examples/eessi-pr-overlap/fetch-prs.sh` writes one JSON file per open
PR. It fetches each PR head into the clone as `refs/remotes/pr/N` and
does not check it out. `--eessi-version` defaults to `2026.06`.

```bash
: "${EESSI_SOFTWARE_PATH:?source the EESSI init script and module load EESSI-extend}"
: "${EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS:?source the EESSI init script and module load EESSI-extend}"
: "${EB_STACK_CHECKOUT:?set this to an eb-stack checkout}"
: "${EB_EASYCONFIGS:?set this to the easyconfig tree for the EasyBuild version these easystacks name}"
: "${EB_EASYBLOCKS:?set this to the easybuild/easyblocks package for that release}"

"$EB_STACK_CHECKOUT/examples/eessi-pr-overlap/fetch-prs.sh" \
  EESSI/software-layer 2026.06 /tmp/pr-overlap-in

find "$EESSI_SOFTWARE_PATH/software" -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 \
  -type d -printf '%P\n' | sort > /tmp/pr-overlap-installed.txt

shopt -s nullglob
args=()
for f in /tmp/pr-overlap-in/prs/*.json; do
  args+=(--pr "$f")
done
for d in /tmp/pr-overlap-in/commit-trees/*/; do
  args+=(--commit-tree "$(basename "$d")=$d")
done
for d in /tmp/pr-overlap-in/easyblocks/*/; do
  args+=(--easyblocks-commit "$(basename "$d")=$d")
done
shopt -u nullglob

eb-stack pr-overlap "${args[@]}" \
  --easyconfigs "$EB_EASYCONFIGS" \
  --easyblocks "$EB_EASYBLOCKS" \
  --installed /tmp/pr-overlap-installed.txt \
  --installed-modulerc "$EESSI_SOFTWARE_PATH/modules/all" \
  --filter-deps "$EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS" \
  --installed-label x86_64/amd/zen4 \
  --eessi-version 2026.06 \
  --exclude-path /accel/ \
  --exclude-path /additional_arch/ \
  --merge-order \
  --out-dir /tmp/pr-overlap-out
```

`nullglob` keeps an empty `commit-trees/` or `easyblocks/` from being
passed as a literal path. You get the same kinds of report files as in
the recorded run. The current PRs and the installed prefix set the
counts and module names. Installed modules drop out of each build set.
`shared_modules` then counts the uninstalled modules in two or more
build sets.

| Flag | What to pass |
| --- | --- |
| `--easyconfigs` | The easyconfigs tree for the EasyBuild version the easystack names |
| `--commit-tree C=DIR` | The easyconfigs at one `from-commit` pin C |
| `--easyblocks` | That EasyBuild release's `easybuild/easyblocks` package |
| `--easyblocks-commit C=DIR` | The easyblock files one `include-easyblocks-from-commit` touches |
| `--installed-modulerc` | The prefix's `modules/all`, so Lmod aliases count as installed |
| `--filter-deps` | Dependencies EasyBuild filters. Defaults to `$EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS` |

# See what the bot builds on each architecture

The EESSI bot builds more than the lines a PR adds. The bot reads
each changed easystack at the PR head. It then builds every entry not
yet installed on that architecture, plus the missing dependencies of
those entries. An entry can sit in the shared easystack for months and
still be missing on one architecture. Every later PR that touches the
file makes that bot try it again. Software-layer PR 1775 did not add GDRCopy.
The riscv64 bot still failed on it.

Pass `--arch-installed ARCH=FILE` once per architecture to get that
build set. The file is the same installed-module list as
`--installed`, and the flag replaces `--installed`. `--bot-build-set`
gives the same whole-file closure for a single `--installed` list.
Without either flag the command closes only the added lines, as in the
recorded run above.

This fixture has the shape of PR 1775. The shared easystack already
lists GDRCopy. PR 1775 adds nvtop, and PR 1800 adds likwid. x86_64 has
GDRCopy installed and riscv64 does not.

```bash
eb-stack pr-overlap \
  --pr tests/pr_overlap_arch/prs.json \
  --easyconfigs tests/pr_overlap_arch/release \
  --arch-installed x86_64=tests/pr_overlap_arch/x86_64.txt \
  --arch-installed riscv64=tests/pr_overlap_arch/riscv64.txt \
  --generated-at 2026-10-30T00:00:00Z \
  --repo-url https://github.com/EESSI/software-layer \
  --merge-order \
  --out-dir /tmp/pr-overlap-arch
```

The command prints:

```
prs=2 records=2 shared_modules=2 skipped_easyconfigs=0 out=/tmp/pr-overlap-arch
```

`overlap.md` now has one section per architecture. On x86_64 the
shared table says `None.` and each PR builds only its own module. Here is
the riscv64 section, trimmed:

```text
| `GDRCopy/2.5.2-GCCcore-15.2.0` | [#1775](https://github.com/EESSI/software-layer/pull/1775), [#1800](https://github.com/EESSI/software-layer/pull/1800) |
| `Lib/1.0-GCCcore-15.2.0` | [#1775](https://github.com/EESSI/software-layer/pull/1775), [#1800](https://github.com/EESSI/software-layer/pull/1800) |

Already in the changed easystack and not installed: `GDRCopy/2.5.2-GCCcore-15.2.0`.
```

The "Already in the changed easystack" line means the PR did not add
GDRCopy, and the riscv64 bot will still build it. Lib comes along
because it is a dependency of GDRCopy. If that architecture cannot
build the module at all, fix the easystack or mark it unsupported
before you merge (see
[refuse a plan an architecture cannot build](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/arch-unsupported.html.md)).
The Merge order table is repeated per architecture. On riscv64, PR 1775
goes first and saves GDRCopy and Lib for PR 1800. In `prs/1775.toml`,
`entries` is still only the nvtop line, and GDRCopy is listed under
`carried`. The per-architecture fields are in
[output formats](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../reference/formats.html.md).

# Wire it into CI

The draft workflow is
`examples/eessi-pr-overlap/pr_dependency_overlap.yml`. It is not
installed in the EESSI software-layer repository from this checkout.

On that repository:

1. Exempt `gh_action_pr_dependency_overlap` from the branch push
   restriction, the same way
   `gh_action_update_software_layer_commit_sha` is exempt, so
   `github-actions[bot]` can push to that one branch. `main` stays
   protected.
2. Copy `pr_dependency_overlap.yml` to `.github/workflows/` and
   `fetch-prs.sh` to
   `.github/workflows/scripts/fetch_pr_easystacks.sh`.
3. Set `EB_STACK_VERSION` and `EB_STACK_SHA256` in the workflow to a
   release that carries `pr-overlap`.

The workflow runs on a schedule and on `workflow_dispatch`, from
`main`. It mounts the stack, writes `overlap.md`, `overlap.toml`, and
one `prs/<N>.toml` per recorded PR, then pushes that report to
`gh_action_pr_dependency_overlap` without force. It opens no pull
request and posts no comment. The publish job skips the commit when only
the `generated_at = ` and `Computed ` lines change. A timestamp-only change is not committed. A title
change is. `--impact` and `--merged` exit 2 and name the number
when it is not in the input. Exclusion wins: a path that matches both
`--include-path` and `--exclude-path` is skipped.

# Easyconfigs pull requests

For open PRs on easybuild-easyconfigs, pass `--kind easyconfigs`. You
do not need `--installed`: the build set is then the modules the base
tree does not already have. The recorded open set is
`tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/`.

```bash
eb-stack pr-overlap \
  --kind easyconfigs \
  --pr tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/prs.json \
  --easyconfigs tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/tree \
  --generated-at 2026-10-24T00:00:00Z \
  --repo-url https://github.com/easybuilders/easybuild-easyconfigs \
  --out-dir /tmp/ec-open-out
```

The command prints:

```
prs=4 records=4 shared_modules=1 skipped_easyconfigs=0 out=/tmp/ec-open-out
```

22823 and 24575 share `Mathematica/14.2.1`. That run, including the
live fetch, is in
[find open easybuild-easyconfigs pull requests that add the same software](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/easyconfigs-pr-overlap.html.md).

# Find open easybuild-easyconfigs pull requests that add the same software

Two open pull requests (PRs) on easybuild-easyconfigs sometimes add the
same easyconfig, or need the same new dependency.
`eb-stack pr-overlap --kind easyconfigs` reads the changed `.eb` files
and reports the new modules each PR would build. The report then names
each file and module that two or more PRs add. Compare those pull
requests before you merge.

Run it before you merge a batch of open easybuild-easyconfigs PRs, or when
a review needs to see whether another open PR already adds the same
software. The command reads easyconfig text as data and leaves the pull
requests untouched. Two build jobs that install into the same prefix
can overwrite a shared module: the later install wins.

For each PR, dependency resolution starts with the tree passed through
`--easyconfigs`. Easyconfigs from the other input PRs are also visible,
below the current PR's own changes. This lets the report detect when
one PR supplies a dependency needed by another.

# Run the recorded pull requests

`tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/` records four open PRs from
2026-10-24. The files under `tree/` are a subset of easybuild-easyconfigs
at the commit named in `develop-sha`, enough to follow the dependencies
of these four PRs.

```bash
eb-stack pr-overlap --kind easyconfigs \
  --pr tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/prs.json \
  --easyconfigs tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/tree \
  --generated-at 2026-10-24T00:00:00Z \
  --repo-url https://github.com/easybuilders/easybuild-easyconfigs \
  --merge-order \
  --out-dir /tmp/ec-order-out
```

It prints one line and exits 0.

```
prs=4 records=4 shared_modules=1 skipped_easyconfigs=0 out=/tmp/ec-order-out
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `prs` | Pull requests read. |
| `records` | Pull requests that changed an easyconfig. |
| `shared_modules` | Modules in more than one build set. |
| `skipped_easyconfigs` | Easyconfig files in the tree the parser could not read. |
| `out` | Directory with the Markdown report, the index, and the per-PR records. |

This run passes no `--installed` list. The build set is then every
closure module missing from the base tree, plus every easyconfig the PR
edits. The run writes
`/tmp/ec-order-out/overlap.md`, `overlap.toml`, `merge-order.toml`,
and one `prs/<N>.toml` per PR. After a short header, `overlap.md` names the
shared file first.

```text
## same-file

| Path | Pull requests |
|---|---|
| `easybuild/easyconfigs/m/Mathematica/Mathematica-14.2.1.eb` | [#22823](https://github.com/easybuilders/easybuild-easyconfigs/pull/22823), [#24575](https://github.com/easybuilders/easybuild-easyconfigs/pull/24575) |

```

# Read the report

A PR's closure is every module its changed easyconfigs depend on,
directly or through other dependencies. The build set (`to_build`) is
the modules it would still build. With no installed list, that is the
modules the base tree does not already have ("new" in the report) and
the easyconfigs the PR edits. The
same terms for an easystack line are in
[from one easystack line to a build set](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../explanation/pr-overlap.html.md).

Start with the four sections at the top of `overlap.md`. Then read the
section for the PR under review.

- `same-file` means two PRs change the same path. Here 22823 and 24575
  both add `Mathematica-14.2.1.eb`. Compare the file contents and review
  status, choose the PR to keep, then close or rebase the duplicate
  before merging.
- `same-module` means two PRs produce the same module name, even if
  their paths differ. Compare the recipes and coordinate the PRs so
  only the intended recipe is built and installed.
- `shared-new-module` is a module that is new in more than one closure.
  The next section of the report repeats `Mathematica/14.2.1`, because
  the base tree does not already provide it. That is the one module
  counted in `shared_modules`.
- `depends-on` is `None` in this run. A row there means one PR has to
  wait for another open PR. Either the other PR adds a module this
  PR's closure needs, or it edits or deletes a module this PR builds a
  dependent of. The PR that adds or edits the module comes first.

The summary line below each PR heading reports how many easyconfigs
changed, how many modules the dependency walk reached, how many are new
to the base tree, and how many would be built. In that line, "new"
means the base tree does not already contain the module, while "Builds"
is the build set. With no installed list, a large closure can still
build one module.

22823 and 24575 each have a closure of one new module,
`Mathematica/14.2.1`. 27131 adds aria2: closure 53, one new,
`aria2/1.37.0-GCCcore-15.2.0`. 27215 changes four nghttp3 easyconfigs.
All four are in its build set: one added file, and three edited files
that the base tree already has. An edited easyconfig is always rebuilt, so it
stays in the build set even though it is not new. The closure has 152
modules and one new module, `nghttp3/1.13.1-GCCcore-13.2.0`, which needs
`CUnit ==2.1-3`. The build list still names that module, and the
requirement is `unresolved`. Until an easyconfig for that CUnit version
is in the tree, treat the build set as incomplete. Look for an open PR
that adds CUnit, or ask the author to add it. The reverse-dependents
line shows what the edits affect, for example
``nghttp2/1.69.0-GCCcore-15.2.0` (1, no-rebuild)`. The number is how
many dependency hops that module is from the changed file: 1 means it
depends on it directly. The word is the rebuild class. `must-rebuild`
dependents join the build set, while `review` and `no-rebuild` ones are
listed for you to check. Every dependent here is `no-rebuild`. The checked-in copy of
this run is `tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/expected/overlap.md`.

Investigate every `unresolved` item before relying on a closure. Review
reverse dependents as compatibility and rebuild candidates. A closure or a
proposed order does not show that an easyconfig builds or passes its
tests.

A closure also counts modules that are already installed. To drop
those from the build set, pass `--installed` with one `Name/version`
per line. Each run rewrites `prs/` to hold only the PRs
of that run.

# Fetch open pull requests

`examples/easyconfigs-pr-overlap/fetch-prs.sh` in the eb-stack checkout
writes one JSON file per open PR that changes an easyconfig. Run it
from a clone of easybuild-easyconfigs whose `origin` is that
repository, with `gh` authenticated for public reads. Set
`EB_STACK_CHECKOUT` to the eb-stack checkout. The script reads base
text from `develop` and does not check a PR out.

```bash
: "${EB_STACK_CHECKOUT:?set this to an eb-stack checkout}"
"$EB_STACK_CHECKOUT/examples/easyconfigs-pr-overlap/fetch-prs.sh" \
  easybuilders/easybuild-easyconfigs /tmp/ec-in
```

Pass `/tmp/ec-in/prs/*.json` as `--pr`, with `--easyconfigs` set to a
checkout of the base tree. `--base-ref` selects the base-file text
downloaded by `--open` and defaults to `develop`. It does not select or
validate the checkout passed through `--easyconfigs`. Use a checkout
and a base ref for the same revision. `--repo-url` defaults to
`https://github.com/easybuilders/easybuild-easyconfigs` for this kind.
If `EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS` is set and you omit `--filter-deps`, the
command drops those dependencies. The recorded run had the variable
unset.

`--open OWNER/NAME` reads the open PRs over HTTPS. When
`GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GH_TOKEN` is set, the command sends it to
api.github.com. Without a token GitHub allows 60 API calls an hour, and
the command makes at least one call per open PR, so an unauthenticated
run suits a repository with a few dozen open PRs at most. For
easybuild-easyconfigs, which has hundreds, set a token or use
`fetch-prs.sh` above. This command writes the same report, fetched by
`--open`:

```bash
eb-stack pr-overlap --kind easyconfigs \
  --open easybuilders/easybuild-easyconfigs \
  --easyconfigs "$EB_EASYCONFIGS" \
  --out-dir /tmp/ec-live
```

# Choose a merge order

`--merge-order` on the command above writes `merge-order.toml` and
appends this table to `overlap.md`:

```text
## Merge order

| Position | PR | Builds | Saves | After |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [#22823](https://github.com/easybuilders/easybuild-easyconfigs/pull/22823) | 1 | [#24575](https://github.com/easybuilders/easybuild-easyconfigs/pull/24575) (`Mathematica/14.2.1`) |  |
| 2 | [#24575](https://github.com/easybuilders/easybuild-easyconfigs/pull/24575) | 0 |  |  |
| 3 | [#27131](https://github.com/easybuilders/easybuild-easyconfigs/pull/27131) | 1 |  |  |
| 4 | [#27215](https://github.com/easybuilders/easybuild-easyconfigs/pull/27215) | 4 |  |  |
```

Builds is how many modules that PR still has left to build once earlier
rows are done. Position 1 builds `Mathematica/14.2.1`. In the Saves cell,
PR 24575 drops that module, and position 2 has nothing left to
build. That row is the `same-file` duplicate: compare
the files, keep one PR, and close or rebase the other. It is not a
second module to install. Position 3 builds aria2, and position 4 builds the four nghttp3 modules.
After is blank because no PR needs a module that only another open PR
adds. When a `depends-on` row exists, After names the PR that adds or
edits the module, and `--impact` on that PR lists the module under
`resolves`. 27215 edits three nghttp3 files. No other PR here builds
a dependent of them, so no row starts at 27215. When two or more
PRs could go next, the fewest modules left to
build wins, then the lowest PR number. Module names are in
`merge-order.toml`.

`--impact N` writes `merge-impact.toml` for that PR alone. For easystack
changes on a European Environment for Scientific Software
Installations (EESSI) software-layer repository, and for the
`--impact` fields, see
[find shared builds across open pull requests](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/pr-overlap.html.md).

# What an in-place patch forces EESSI to rebuild

Goal: the patched easyconfigs keep their filenames and versions. Report
which installed modules must be rebuilt, which need a review, and which
link the patched package as a shared library. The set is the rebuild
closure: every installed module that depends on the patched one within
its toolchain generation, and no module from another generation.

# Run it on the fixture

```bash
eb-stack rebuild-set \
  --changed tests/rebuild_set_fixtures/changed.txt \
  --easystack tests/rebuild_set_fixtures/eessi-2026.06-eb-5.4.0-2026.1.yml \
  --easystack tests/rebuild_set_fixtures/20261001-eb-5.4.1-zlib.yml \
  --easyconfigs tests/rebuild_set_fixtures/release \
  --easyblocks tests/rebuild_set_fixtures/easyblocks \
  --installed tests/rebuild_set_fixtures/installed.txt \
  --installed-modulerc tests/rebuild_set_fixtures/modules/all \
  --installed-label x86_64/amd/zen4 \
  --generated-at 2026-10-22T12:00:00Z \
  --out-dir /tmp/rebuild-out
```

The command prints:

```
changed=2 rows=8 must-rebuild=2 review=2 no-rebuild=4 missing=1 easystacks=2 skipped_easyconfigs=0 out=/tmp/rebuild-out
```

# Run it on a mounted stack

From a clone of `EESSI/software-layer`, with the 2026.06 stack mounted.
`EB_EASYCONFIGS` and `EB_EASYBLOCKS` come from
`scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh`:

```bash
scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh
set -a
source "${EB_UPSTREAM_CACHE:-$HOME/.cache/eb-stack/upstream}/env.sh"
set +a
eb-stack rebuild-set \
  --changed changed.txt \
  --easystack easystacks/software.eessi.io/2026.06/*.yml \
  --easystack easystacks/software.eessi.io/2026.06/rebuilds/*.yml \
  $(for d in commit-trees/*/; do printf -- '--commit-tree %s=%s ' "$(basename "$d")" "$d"; done) \
  --easyconfigs "$EB_EASYCONFIGS" \
  --easyblocks "$EB_EASYBLOCKS" \
  --installed installed.txt \
  --installed-modulerc "$EESSI_SOFTWARE_PATH/modules/all" \
  --filter-deps "$EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS" \
  --installed-label x86_64/amd/zen4 \
  --generated-at 2026-10-22T12:00:00Z \
  --out-dir /tmp/rebuild-out
```

`--commit-tree NAME=DIR` resolves a `from-commit` pin, the same way as
`pr-overlap`. `--filter-deps` drops dependency tuples before the walk.
When the flag is omitted and `EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS` is set, the command
reads the variable. `--prefix` is an install prefix: for each patched
module the command reads `software/<name>/<version>/lib**/**.a` there.
`--check-static` needs `--prefix`.

`--changed` is an easyconfig filename, repeated, or a file that is not an
`.eb`: one filename per line, blank lines and `#` comments skipped.
`--easystack` is each deployed easystack. A `from-commit` pin is resolved
with `--commit-tree`, the same way as `pr-overlap`. Pass the CPU
easystacks for the target you are asking about, and leave out `accel/`
and `additional_arch/` unless that is the stack you mounted.

`--easyconfigs` is the easyconfigs tree of the EasyBuild release the
stack uses. `--filter-deps` drops dependency tuples before the walk, with
the same matching as `pr-overlap`. It does not remove an extension from a
bundle's `exts_list`. When the flag is omitted and `EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS`
is set, the command reads the variable. `--installed-modulerc` is that
prefix's `modules/all`. `--easyblocks` is the EasyBuild release's
`easybuild/easyblocks` package. A missing class is recorded. The module
stays in the set, because it is already installed.

# Rank scanner findings by rebuild cost

A scanner export names the modules that carry a vulnerable package. Pass
it as `--findings` instead of `--changed`. A site that installs from build
lists has no easystack, so leave `--easystack` out: the installed list is
the stack.

```bash
eb-stack rebuild-set \
  --findings tests/rebuild_set_fixtures/findings.csv \
  --easyconfigs tests/rebuild_set_fixtures/release \
  --installed tests/rebuild_set_fixtures/installed.txt \
  --installed-label x86_64/amd/zen4 \
  --generated-at 2026-10-22T12:00:00Z \
  --out-dir /tmp/findings-out
```

The command prints:

```
changed=2 rows=10 must-rebuild=3 review=2 no-rebuild=5 missing=0 easystacks=1 skipped_easyconfigs=0 findings_modules=2 out=/tmp/findings-out
```

`findings.md` ranks each module by weighted score per in-place rebuild:

```
| Rank | Module | Highest | C | H | M | L | Fixed | Score | In place | Bump | Value |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `zlib/1.3.1-GCCcore-15.2.0` | Critical | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 1/2 | 11 | 4 | 8 | 2.75 |
| 2 | `libpng/1.6.50-GCCcore-15.2.0` | High | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1/1 | 5 | 2 | 3 | 2.50 |
```

A backported zlib patch rebuilds 4 modules; a zlib version bump rebuilds 8.

# Read the three files

`out/rebuild-set.md` is the table: changed easyconfig, dependent, edge
kind, class, and reason, then the counts. A changed filename that is not
in the deployed graph is listed and has no row. `out/rebuild-set.json` is
the same document.

`out/rebuilds/<YYYYMMDD>-eb-<version>-cve-patches.yml` lists class
must-rebuild only, with `rebuild: true`. The date is taken from
`--generated-at` (or from the current date in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)). One file per EasyBuild
version named by the easystack filenames. A second run replaces the
`rebuilds/*.yml` files from the previous run.

`--prefix` is `$EESSI_SOFTWARE_PATH`. For each patched module the command
reads `software/<name>/<version>/lib**/**.a`. A patched module with
no static archive cannot have been linked statically, so a
builddependency-only dependent is no-rebuild and the reason is ~no static
archive installed~. Archives that are installed keep the row in review
and are named. A missing install directory is a note, and the row stays
in review. A prefix with no `software` directory is an error.

A review dependent is one row. The changed column lists every patched
easyconfig that put it there.

`--check-static` needs `--prefix`. For each remaining review dependent it
reads defined dynamic symbols, the names `nm -D --defined-only` prints,
from the installed Executable and Linkable Format (ELF) files. The patched library's names come from its
shared objects, or from the archive members when the install has no
shared object. A hit is must-rebuild. No hit is no-rebuild. An empty export set
stays in review, because there was nothing to look for.

The symbol scan can go wrong. It sees dynamic symbols only, so a hidden,
local, or inlined static link is a false no-rebuild. A short name shared
with another library is a false must-rebuild. Scripts, bytecode, and
libraries opened with dlopen are invisible. A static archive shows that a
static link was possible, not that it happened.

Why a runtime dependency needs no rebuild, and why a bundle extension
does, is covered in
[what an in-place patch forces a rebuild of](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../explanation/rebuild-set.html.md).

# Which modules carry a component, and what that forces rebuilt

Goal: a Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) record names a component and a version. List every easyconfig and
installed module in one toolchain generation that carries it, then feed
the recipes that contain it into the rebuild closure.

# Run it

The recorded slice in this checkout is enough to see the counts. The
files are copies of easybuild-easyconfigs develop
`981d2123dddccca9ce0b15f9eb2643e872332f5e`, the pin in
`scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh`, and the upstream `LICENSE` is in
that directory.

```bash
eb-stack component-reach \
  --component curl \
  --version '>=8,<9' \
  --generation 2026.1 \
  --easyconfigs tests/component_reach_recorded \
  --out-dir /tmp/component-reach
```

The command prints:

```
component=curl version=>=8,<9 generation=2026.1 carriers=2 changed=1 must-rebuild=1 review=0 no-rebuild=1 out=/tmp/component-reach
```

cURL 8.17.0 is the module. git 2.52.0 depends on that cURL and is the
no-rebuild row. The same command against the pinned easyconfigs tree
and a deployed easystack uses `scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh`. Pass
one of `--component`, `--purl`, or `--cve`.

```bash
scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh
set -a
source "${EB_UPSTREAM_CACHE:-$HOME/.cache/eb-stack/upstream}/env.sh"
set +a
eb-stack component-reach \
  --component curl \
  --version '>=8,<9' \
  --generation 2026.1 \
  --easyconfigs "$EB_EASYCONFIGS" \
  --easystack "$EB_EESSI_SOFTWARE_LAYER/easystacks/software.eessi.io/2026.06/eessi-2026.06-eb-5.4.0-2026.1.yml" \
  --out-dir /tmp/component-reach-full
```

The command prints:

```
component=curl version=>=8,<9 generation=2026.1 carriers=23 changed=2 must-rebuild=1 review=106 no-rebuild=16 out=/tmp/component-reach-full
```

The changed files are `cURL-8.17.0-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb` and
`cargo-c-0.10.23-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb`. The must-rebuild row is
`cURL/8.17.0-GCCcore-15.2.0`, reason `patched easyconfig`.

`--easystack` and `--installed` narrow the walk to a deployed prefix.
`--filter-deps` drops dependency tuples before the closure walk. When
that flag is omitted and `EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS` is set, the command
reads the variable. The recorded command above passes neither, so every
easyconfig in the generation is the stack.

`--component` is the name. Matching ignores ASCII letter case, so `curl` matches
`cURL` and `jupyterlab` matches `JupyterLab`. The match is a whole token,
so `jupyterlab` does not match `jupyterlab-server` and `curl` does not
match `libcurl`.

`--version` is an exact version, `*` for any version, or a requirement
such as `>=8,<9`. It is required with `--component`. With `--purl` it
replaces the version in the URL. `--cve` does not take `--version`: the
versions come from Open Source Vulnerabilities (OSV).

`--purl` is a package URL, for example
`pkg:cargo/rustls-webpki@0.102.8` or `pkg:pypi/urllib3@2.5.0`. The type
selects which carriers count. `generic` and `github` match the
easyconfig name: the module, a dependency, a builddependency, a
component, a source, or a patch. `pypi`, `cargo`, `npm`, `golang`, and
`cran` match an extension or a bundled component of that language.
`cargo` also matches a crate, and `pypi` also matches a wheel. Any
other type is rejected: the command exits 2 and the error says that
purl type has no carrier model. `pkg:cargo/curl` and `pkg:npm/curl` do
not match the cURL easyconfig. `--component curl` still matches that
recipe by name. A version in the URL is the requirement unless
`--version` is also passed.

`--cve` is a CVE id or another OSV id. The record is fetched from
`https://api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/<id>`. A CVE record often has only a git
range and no package. Advisory aliases (`GHSA-`, `RUSTSEC-`, `PYSEC-`,
`GO-`) are followed, up to eight. Named tags such as `libXpm-3.5.17`
become exact versions. Git tags such as `XORG-6_8_0` do not. Each
affected package is searched on its own, and a version matches when any
of that package's requirements match or when it is one of the exact
versions. A range whose type is not SEMVER or ECOSYSTEM, and an event
that does not parse as a version requirement, is listed under
Unresolved ranges in the markdown. It is not discarded. When every
range on a package was unparsed, that package counts as review and its
carrier list stays empty. The three output files are then one document
with `kind` set to `cve`, and `results` contains one reach document per
package. The summary line includes the closure counts `changed`,
`must-rebuild`, `review`, and `no-rebuild`.

`--generation` is the toolchain generation, for example `2026.1` or
`2025a`. A recipe is in that generation when its toolchain version is
that string, or when its toolchain is a member of the known foss
hierarchy for that generation. `GCCcore-15.2.0` and `GCC-15.2.0` belong
to `2026.1`. `GCCcore-14.2.0` belongs to `2025a`, `GCCcore-14.3.0` to
`2025b`, and `GCCcore-13.3.0` to `2024a`. A system toolchain does not. A
module built with another generation is not a row.

`--easystack-url` repeats. The URL must be `https://`. The body is an
easystack, read the same way as `--easystack`. Local files and URLs are
one stack.

# What carries it

- the easyconfig's own module name and version;
- a `dependencies` or `builddependencies` tuple;
- a bundle `components` entry;
- a Python, R, or Perl extension in `exts_list`;
- a Cargo crate, from a `crates` tuple or from a filename such as
  `libz-sys-1.1.29.tar.gz`, including a vendored `+name-version` fragment
  such as `0.4.89+curl-8.20.0`. A Cargo recipe also matches a crate that
  appears only as a checksum key, such as `rustls-webpki-0.102.8.tar.gz`.
  The recipe's own tarball is not that crate;
- a Python wheel: a `.whl` filename in `sources` or `checksums`, an
  `exts_list` entry whose source is a wheel (`pastel`), or a top-level
  `source_tmpl` that names a wheel (`cleo`). The role is `wheel`;
- a vendored or bundled filename in `sources` or `patches` whose name
  contains the component and a version;
- a line in `--compat-layer`, `name version` or `name==version`, `#`
  comments skipped.

A dependency or a builddependency lists the recipe as a carrier and does
not add it to the patched set. The component's own module is the root,
and those recipes are its closure. A module, bundle component, extension,
crate, source, or patch means the recipe contains the bytes, and that
filename is a patched root.

The compat layer is not an easyconfig. Pass it with `--compat-layer`. A
hit is a row with an empty easyconfig and a note that it has no rebuild
edge.

`--filter-deps` drops dependency tuples before the closure walk, the same
way as `rebuild-set`, and does not strip `exts_list`. When the flag is
omitted and `EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS` is set, the command reads it.

# The closure

With no `--easystack`, every easyconfig in the generation is the stack.
With no `--installed`, every module in the generation is treated as
installed, so the reverse walk does not stop. Pass both when the question
is a mounted prefix: then only those modules are visited.

The closure is the rebuild set of the containing recipes, inside the
generation. Classes are the same as `rebuild-set`: `must-rebuild`,
`review`, and `no-rebuild`. This command does not read a prefix or scan
static symbols.

# Read the three files

`out/component-reach.md` is the carrier table and the closure table.
`out/component-reach.json` is the same document.
`out/component-reach.toml` starts with
`# Generated by `eb-stack component-reach`.`
Schema version 1. See [output formats](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../reference/formats.html.md).

# Find from-commit pins an EasyBuild release already contains

An easystack can select an easyconfig from a specific
easybuild-easyconfigs commit with `from-commit`. You add the pin when
that file is newer than the EasyBuild release the stack uses. Once a
later release contains the commit, check the file too. A later commit
may have changed it, and then removing the pin changes the build. `eb-stack stack from-commit`
reports whether each pin commit is in the release and whether the
pinned file is identical to the release file.

Run it before you delete `from-commit` lines after an EasyBuild
release. A CI job can fail on the same command. Exit status 1 means a
pin is already in the release, or that the check itself failed. The
counts line tells those two apart.

# Check one pin

Save this fixture as `/tmp/20261011-eb-5.4.0-UCX.yml`. The file name
contains `eb-5.4.0`, so omit `--easybuild-version`. The pin is the
commit that merged a fix to the Unified Communication X library, easybuild-easyconfigs pull request 24388.
`$EB_EASYCONFIGS` is a clone of easybuild-easyconfigs that has the tag
`easybuild-easyconfigs-v5.4.0`. A blobless clone (`git clone` with
`--filter=blob:none`) is enough once it contains the pin commit and
that tag. `scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh` clones v5.4.1, and that
clone still has the v5.4.0 tag.

```yaml
easyconfigs:
  - UCX-1.18.0-GCCcore-14.2.0.eb:
      options:
        from-commit: d438adc699f5ff35d866d9045f0aae663a0913cb
```

```bash
cd /tmp
eb-stack stack from-commit \
  --easystack 20261011-eb-5.4.0-UCX.yml \
  --easyconfigs-repo "$EB_EASYCONFIGS"
```

That command printed:

```
status=released blob=differs version=5.4.0 tag=easybuild-easyconfigs-v5.4.0 kind=from-commit commit=d438adc699f5ff35d866d9045f0aae663a0913cb file=UCX-1.18.0-GCCcore-14.2.0.eb easystack=20261011-eb-5.4.0-UCX.yml
pins=1 released=1 newer=0 unknown=0
```

The process exited 1. Standard error was:

```
error: 1 from-commit pin(s) already in the EasyBuild release
```

`released` means the pin commit is an ancestor of the tag
`easybuild-easyconfigs-v5.4.0`. A commit is an ancestor of itself, so a
pin of the tag commit is `released` too. `blob=same` means the file at
the pin and the file in the release have the same bytes.
`blob=differs` means they are not. This file changed once in between:
commit `0c9d4a8a28a0` added the glibc 2.43 patch to
`UCX-1.18.0-GCCcore-14.2.0.eb`. The last line counts the pins in each
state.

Compare the two files with:

```bash
git -C "$EB_EASYCONFIGS" diff --unified=0 d438adc699f5ff35d866d9045f0aae663a0913cb easybuild-easyconfigs-v5.4.0 \
  -- easybuild/easyconfigs/u/UCX/UCX-1.18.0-GCCcore-14.2.0.eb
```

That command printed:

```
diff --git a/easybuild/easyconfigs/u/UCX/UCX-1.18.0-GCCcore-14.2.0.eb b/easybuild/easyconfigs/u/UCX/UCX-1.18.0-GCCcore-14.2.0.eb
index 6c73e9f0df..cff427c9dc 100644
--- a/easybuild/easyconfigs/u/UCX/UCX-1.18.0-GCCcore-14.2.0.eb
+++ b/easybuild/easyconfigs/u/UCX/UCX-1.18.0-GCCcore-14.2.0.eb
@@ -19,0 +20 @@ patches = [
+    'UCX-1.18.0_fix-glibc-2.43-compile-failure.patch',
@@ -24,0 +26,2 @@ checksums = [
+    {'UCX-1.18.0_fix-glibc-2.43-compile-failure.patch':
+     'c67b2070a65e8217b7c6f9d9a6a13ff11141bacfed395d551376432428348a9c'},
```

Removing the pin switches the build to the release file. Here the
release file has the pinned fix plus a later glibc 2.43 patch, so
removing the pin is the normal choice. Keep the pin only if the
build depends on the file exactly as pinned.

| What the line says | What you do |
| --- | --- |
| `released` and `blob=same` | Remove the pin. The release file is the pinned file. |
| `released` and `blob=differs` | Compare the pinned file with the release file. Remove the pin only if the release version is the one to build; otherwise keep the pin and document why. |
| `newer` | The commit exists but is not an ancestor of the release tag. Despite the label, it may be later or on another line of history. Keep the pin unless you verify that the intended recipe is available another way. |
| `unknown` | Read `reason`. `reason`commit-missing` or `reason`tag-missing` names what to fetch. `unknown` on its own exits 0 and is not evidence that the pin is still needed. |

`newer` and `unknown` lines have no `blob` field. `differs` also means
the filename is missing on one side, or the filename matches more than
one path. A `released` pin with `blob=same` still exits 1. Remove the
pin when you want exit 0, or pass `--rewrite`. `--rewrite` deletes
each `released` pin with `blob=same` from the easystack in place,
prints those rows as `status`dropped`, adds a `rewritten`N` line, and
exits 0. It leaves every other pin in the file.

# Exit status

| Exit | When |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | No pin is `released`: every pin is `newer` or `unknown`, or the files have no pins. |
| 1 | A pin is `released` and `--rewrite` is not set (standard error: `N from-commit pin(s) already in the EasyBuild release`), or the check failed: an easystack that cannot be read, a `--easyconfigs-repo` that is not a git checkout, or a git error. |
| 2 | Bad command line: no `--easystack` flag, a version not in `X.Y.Z` form, a file with pins but no `eb-X.Y.Z` in its name and no `--easybuild-version`, or no `--easyconfigs-repo` / `--easyblocks-repo` flag when a pin needs one. |

In CI, tell the two kinds of exit 1 apart by the counts line. A
released pin prints `pins`... released`N` on standard output, and a
failed check prints no counts line. `unknown` exits 0, so also fail
the job when `unknown=` is not 0. On a partial clone, a missing commit
can make git try to download it. That exits 1 with the git error and
no counts line. A pin-free easystack needs neither a version nor
repository arguments and reports zero pins.

# Flags

`--easybuild-version 5.4.0` sets the release. When the flag is omitted,
the command reads `eb-X.Y.Z` from the file name. The flag overrides the
file name. The easyconfigs tag is `easybuild-easyconfigs-vX.Y.Z` in
`--easyconfigs-repo`. The check reads object hashes from git tree
metadata. The blobless clone above is enough for that.

Pass `--easyblocks-repo` only when an entry sets
`include-easyblocks-from-commit`. The tag is
`easybuild-easyblocks-vX.Y.Z`. For these pins `blob` compares two whole
trees, at the pin and at the tag. `same` means the whole easyblocks repository is
identical at the pin and the tag, which is rare. Expect `differs` for
these pins and compare the easyblock files the pin added.

Repeat `--easystack` for more than one file. Each pin is one line, and
the commit text is the text from the easystack. `--json` prints the
same fields as JSON. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool
`eb_stack_from_commit` returns that report. A `from-commit` pin also
changes what `pr-overlap` builds: pass that commit's tree as
`--commit-tree`. See
[find shared builds across open pull requests](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/pr-overlap.html.md).

After changing the easystack, rerun `stack from-commit`, then run the
normal EasyBuild easystack dry run. Commit containment and blob
equality are source checks, not build evidence.

# Refuse a plan an architecture cannot build

What it does: `stack arch` reads an easystack as a plan. With
`--easyconfigs` it also closes the dependencies. An entry the
architecture cannot build fails the command. The message names that
entry and the architecture.

Why you'd use it: a shared EESSI easystack is built on every CPU
architecture. GDRCopy needs CUDA, and its header rejects riscv64.
Software-layer pull request 1775 added other lines to
`eessi-2026.06-eb-5.4.0-2026.1.yml`, and the riscv64 bot failed on the
GDRCopy line that was already there. Pull request 1822 tried GDRCopy
on riscv64 alone and failed the same way. Pull request 1876 failed
bwa-mem2 on aarch64 because the Makefile passes `-msse`.

```bash
eb-stack stack arch \
  --arch riscv64 \
  --easystack tests/arch_unsupported_fixtures/easystacks/eessi-2026.06-eb-5.4.0-2026.1.yml \
  --easyconfigs tests/arch_unsupported_fixtures/easyconfigs \
  --installed tests/arch_unsupported_fixtures/installed-riscv64.txt \
  --additional-arch tests/arch_unsupported_fixtures/additional_arch/riscv64/generic/eessi-2026.06-eb-5.4.0-2026.1.yml
```

The command prints:

```
GDRCopy-2.5.2-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb is unsupported on riscv64: needs CUDA; gdrconfig.h errors with architecture is not supported (software-layer #1775, #1822)
GDRCopy-2.5.2-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb is flagged on riscv64: it has never been installed there and is not in the riscv64 additional_arch easystack
unsupported=1 flagged=1
```

The first line is the hard failure. `GDRCopy-2.5.2-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb` is
the entry. `riscv64` is the architecture. The reason and the pull
request numbers come from `data/arch-unsupported.toml`. The command
exits 1, and the error repeats that line.

The second line is the cheap check, and it does not read recipes. The
entry is in the shared easystack, `--installed` has no
`GDRCopy/2.5.2-GCCcore-15.2.0` line, and `--additional-arch` does not
name the file. `unsupported`` and `flagged`` are the two counts.
`--unsupported` replaces the bundled list.

A plan that only depends on the entry names the depender. This
easystack lists nvtop, and nvtop depends on GDRCopy:

```bash
eb-stack stack arch \
  --arch riscv64 \
  --easystack tests/arch_unsupported_fixtures/easystacks/nvtop-only.yml \
  --easyconfigs tests/arch_unsupported_fixtures/easyconfigs
```

```
GDRCopy-2.5.2-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb is unsupported on riscv64: needs CUDA; gdrconfig.h errors with architecture is not supported (software-layer #1775, #1822) (required by nvtop-3.3.2-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb)
unsupported=1 flagged=0
```

`(required by nvtop-3.3.2-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb)` means the plan did not
name GDRCopy. The closure did. `flagged=0` is the cheap check staying
quiet, because `--installed` was not passed.

bwa-mem2 is the aarch64 entry:

```bash
eb-stack stack arch \
  --arch aarch64 \
  --easystack tests/arch_unsupported_fixtures/easystacks/bwa-mem2.yml \
  --easyconfigs tests/arch_unsupported_fixtures/easyconfigs
```

```
bwa-mem2-2.3-GCC-14.3.0.eb is unsupported on aarch64: the Makefile passes -msse and -msse2, which aarch64 gcc rejects (software-layer #1876)
unsupported=1 flagged=0
```

`--arch aarch64/neoverse_v1` is the same family as `--arch aarch64`.
The family is the text before the first slash. With no `--arch`, every
family in the list is checked. `--arch x86_64` does not reject GDRCopy:
the list has no x86_64 entry for it.

An entry that is in the `additional_arch` easystack is not flagged,
even when it has never been installed. It is still unsupported when
the list says so. Passing `--installed` with more than one `--arch`
needs a prefix, `riscv64=installed-riscv64.txt`. The same prefix form
works for `--additional-arch`. A directory is every easystack under it.

`stack batch` uses the same list before it writes a plan. A root that
includes GDRCopy, or depends on it, exits 1 and does not write
`plan.json`. `--arch` limits that check to one family. With no
`--arch`, every family in the list is checked, because the batch is a
shared easystack.

Software-layer pull request 1623 added waLBerla 7.2. The bot failed on
aarch64 neoverse_v1, a64fx, and nvidia/grace because `SIMDAlignment()`
was not constexpr under SVE. The from-commit pin a69e693 patches that,
and the bot then succeeded on those targets. waLBerla is not in the
list. The cheap check is what flags a shared entry before that first
bot run, while it has never been installed on the architecture and is
not in that architecture's `additional_arch` easystack.

See [the command-line reference](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../reference/cli.html.md).

# Command-line reference

`eb-stack` has six namespaced command groups (`package`, `recipe`,
`stack`, `target`, `campaign`, `repro`), four reports (`easyblock-reach`,
`pr-overlap`, `rebuild-set`, `component-reach`), and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.
`--version` prints the crate version. All paths written by package commands
are deterministic bundle artifacts.

# Exit status

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | The command finished the work it was asked to do |
| 1 | The work was attempted and failed: a missing or unreadable file, a document that does not parse, a check that found errors, a network fetch that failed, a doctor probe, or a campaign whose build failed |
| 2 | The command line was rejected before that work: a missing or unknown flag (clap), or a flag value or combination the command does not accept |

A rejected value names the flag and the value. A missing file names the flag and the path. Status 2 is the same status clap already uses. A recipe that fails `recipe lint` or `recipe check` is status 1: the files were read and the check failed. `stack from-commit` is status 1 when any pin is `released`, and status 0 when every pin is `newer` or `unknown` or the files name no pin. A file name with no `eb-X.Y.Z`, and no `--easybuild-version`, is status 2. `stack arch` is status 1 when an entry is unsupported or flagged. `stack batch` is status 1 when the plan includes, or depends on, an entry the architecture cannot build.

`--help` for every command has an example and a description of every flag. A default that the command applies is printed in that help. A directory that receives several artifacts is `--out-dir`. A single output file is `--out` (`--lock-out` for the lock `stack solve` writes). `--installed`, `--easyconfigs`, `--filter-deps`, and `--generated-at` use those names on every command that takes them.

Package commands take the toolchain as `--toolchain name/version`, the spelling `stack solve` uses. `--toolchain system`, `--toolchain SYSTEM`, and `--toolchain system/` select the SYSTEM toolchain. Its version is empty. `package inspect` and `package plan` accept a lone `--toolchain-version` and use `foss`. `package bump` does not.

# Command map

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `package inspect` | Parse conda-forge, Spack, PyPI, Comprehensive R Archive Network (CRAN), Cargo, LuaRocks, or Raku into a manifest and planned software bill of materials (SBOM) |
| `package plan` | Materialize profiles, solve with Resolvo, and emit recipes |
| `package bump` | Retarget an EasyBuild recipe and write the same canonical bundle |
| `recipe easyblock` | Print the easyblock class name EasyBuild derives for a software name |
| `recipe templates` | Emit template constants and derived-key rules, or the values `--name` and `--version` resolve |
| `recipe hierarchy` | Emit known toolchain hierarchies as JSON |
| `recipe check` | Validate metadata and robot dependency availability |
| `recipe lint` / `recipe format` | Report upstream CI, test-suite, and review findings (E999, F541, W605, W291, E501, E2xx, `EB_*`; `eb --check-contrib` merged when `eb` is installed) or mechanically wrap E501 lines |
| `stack solve` / `stack sbom` | Solve a multi-root stack or emit SBOM from a lock |
| `stack order` | Sequence every pinned build a set of roots needs |
| `stack easystack` | Write a lock as the YAML `eb --easystack` reads |
| `stack sections` | Regroup a Jenkins build list under a previous list's headers |
| `stack from-commit` | Report `from-commit` pins already contained in an EasyBuild release |
| `stack arch` | Refuse a plan an architecture cannot build, and flag entries never installed there |
| `repro summary` | Print a reproduction scoreboard from collected case scores |
| `pr-overlap` | Close open pull-request easystack additions against an installed stack and report shared builds |
| `rebuild-set` | Classify the installed reverse dependents of easyconfigs patched in place |
| `component-reach` | List who carries a component in one generation and close their rebuild set |
| `target list` / `target doctor` | Resolve layered target configuration and probe it |
| `campaign run` / `campaign status` | Execute or inspect a persisted build campaign |
| `campaign finding ...` | Claim and resolve typed build findings |
| `mcp [--workspace]` | Serve each CLI workflow over stdio, including `pr-overlap`, `rebuild-set`, `component-reach`, and `easyblock-reach`, with recipe file tools rooted at `--workspace` |
| `easyblock-reach` | Report easyconfigs and installed modules reached by an easyblock or framework change |

# Package commands

## `package inspect`

```bash
eb-stack package inspect \
  --source PATH \
  --format auto|conda-forge|spack|pypi|cran|cargo|luarocks|raku \
  --toolchain foss/2026.1 \
  [--package-config PACKAGE.toml]... \
  --out-dir BUNDLE
```

This writes `package.plan.json` and `package.sbom.cdx.json`. It does not solve
profiles or emit recipes, so it establishes no claim-ladder rung.

## `package plan`

```bash
eb-stack package plan \
  --source PATH \
  --format auto|conda-forge|spack|pypi|cran|cargo|luarocks|raku \
  --toolchain foss/2026.1 \
  [--package-config PACKAGE.toml]... \
  [--source-checksum DIGEST]... \
  [--package-index FILE] \
  --easyconfigs UPSTREAM \
  [--easyconfigs OVERLAY]... \
  --stack-policy STACK.toml \
  [--package-catalog CATALOG.toml]... \
  [--package-sources SOURCES.toml]... \
  [--easybuild-source DIR]... \
  [--conda-source DIR]... \
  [--spack-source DIR]... \
  [--cargo-source DIR]... \
  --out-dir BUNDLE
```

Package configs apply in argument order; later metadata, build policy, aliases,
and profile values override earlier layers. Later robot paths override earlier paths for the same EasyBuild identity.
`build.patches` replaces the existing patch list by default. Set
`patches_mode = "merge"` in the layer's `[build]` table to retain foreign or
preceding patches while adding or refining artifacts by filename.
Each requested product profile is solved independently and emits one lock plus
one conventional `.eb` file. The default profile has no suffix; non-default
profiles use their declared `versionsuffix`.

Every emitted source needs a SHA-256 checksum. When a foreign recipe provides
only a version control system (VCS) commit, repeat `--source-checksum` once for every source artifact in
manifest order. The values replace the positional source checksums in both the
manifest/SBOM and every emitted recipe. Planning fails before emission when
the count, shape, or completeness is invalid.

`--package-index FILE` supplies a version for a dependency that states none.
The file is either a CRAN `PACKAGES` index or a `name==version` list, one pin
per line. A range is not a version and supplies nothing.

Passing `--easyconfigs` always uses the closure writer, because that tree is
also a discovery root. The bundle then contains `closure.plan.json`,
`closure.sbom.cdx.json`, and `build-order.json` even when no companion was
needed. `--emit-easyblock` does not combine with that writer.

When a direct dependency has no compatible robot candidate, further closure
inputs close the hole without inventing versions:

- `--package-sources` layers ordered EasyBuild / conda-forge / Spack / Cargo roots;
- `--easybuild-source`, `--conda-source`, `--spack-source`, and `--cargo-source` push roots
  without a TOML file (order is discovery order);
- `--package-catalog` layers explicit foreign or `easybuild-bump` providers as
  ordered overrides.
- `--emit-easyblock` renders an easyblock skeleton for the package into
  `easyblocks/<letter>/<module>.py`, writes it next to the recipes, names the
  derived class as the easyblock and moves the variant options out of the
  emitted recipes. Without it a package that owes an easyblock gets a
  `missing-easyblock` residual. It does not combine with closure planning.
  `package bump` takes the same flag.

Robot candidates win over catalog entries. A closed plan writes companion
packages under `packages/`, a shared `easyconfigs/` overlay, topological
`build-order.json`, and `closure.sbom.cdx.json`. See
[package bundles](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/package-bundles.html.md) and the new-package how-to.

`--format cargo` reads `Cargo.toml` or crates.io JSON. A `Cargo.toml` names
no crate tarball, so plan stops with ~foreign package plan has no source
artifacts~. The crates.io JSON carries the checksum, and that is what plan
emits from. A PyPI leftover
whose run dependency is a PyO3 crate is closed by `--cargo-source`, not
by a pip extra. Extra site packages that Warehouse omits belong in the
ingest: a JSON array of Warehouse objects, or later `requirements.txt`
lines. Resolvo then takes the robot module when `--easyconfigs` provides
it. Do not hand-edit the emitted recipe for those names. A PEP 518
`build_system` object with `build-backend = mesonpy` is the mesonpy hint:
listed `requires` become build deps in the Boolean satisfiability (SAT) solve, and the emitter writes
`wrap_mode=default` plus the shared cargo-on-EESSI isolation prelude
(host wrappers off, `LINKER=${CC:-gcc}`, compat `ld` from `uname -m`).
Hatchling stays a `Python-bundle-PyPI` module when the robot provides
it. See [site Python extras](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../howto/pypi-extend.html.md).

## `package bump`

```bash
eb-stack package bump \
  --source RECIPE.eb \
  --toolchain foss/2024a \
  [--version VERSION | --latest [--overrides OVERRIDES.toml]...] \
  [--source-checksum DIGEST] \
  [--dep NAME=VERSION]... \
  --easyconfigs UPSTREAM \
  [--easyconfigs OVERLAY]... \
  [--hierarchy-fixture HIERARCHY.json] \
  [--stack-policy STACK.toml] \
  [--package-config PACKAGE.toml]... \
  [--strict-patches] \
  [--emit-easyblock] \
  [--fetch-checksums] \
  --out-dir BUNDLE
```

A bump writes the same manifest, planned SBOM, profile lock, and recipe layout
as a new package. `--dep` becomes a locked Resolvo override. The solve fails
when that name is not in the robot tree. A name the recipe does not depend on
stays out of the emitted dependency list, and the lock records the pin outcome.
Without `--stack-policy`, the solver uses an unconstrained policy for the
requested toolchain. A changed package version without `--source-checksum`
clears the old digest and produces a visible residual, because source bytes
cannot be inferred safely. `--package-config` is repeatable and applies after
the source recipe is parsed, as it does for `package plan`. `--strict-patches`
fails the bump when a patch's fate across a version change cannot be decided
from the tree, or, with `--fetch-checksums`, from the new source; without it
the patch is carried and a `patch-decision` residual records the review flag.
`--emit-easyblock` is the same flag as on `package plan`.
`--fetch-checksums` downloads each `sources` entry from the recipe's
`source_urls` when the version changed and `--source-checksum` was omitted,
and writes that SHA-256 into the recipe and the SBOM. An archive URL that
404s under the recipe's tag spelling is tried with the leading `v` added or
removed, and the `sources` entry is rewritten to the name that served it. A
later source whose bytes match the digest the recipe states is confirmed. A
git checkout, a missing URL, or a failed download stays empty. The attempts
are `sources.fetch.json` (one object per source: `filename`, `url`, `sha256`,
`errors`, and `respelled` when the tag spelling changed) and a `source:fetch`
residual. With the new source unpacked, each patch the tree cannot decide is
tried the way EasyBuild's patch step applies it (`patch -p<level>` at the
level EasyBuild guesses, in recipe order): a patch that applies is carried,
one that reverse-applies or whose modified files are all gone is dropped from
`patches` and `checksums`, and anything else stays an undecided
`patch-decision` residual naming the failed hunks. The patches of an
extension that is the package itself are tried against its new archive. See
[output formats](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/formats.html.md).
`--latest` takes the version `package latest` picks for the recipe, so it
conflicts with `--version`; `--overrides` adds override files to that
decision. The bump fails when no stable release survives.

## `package latest`

```bash
eb-stack package latest \
  --source RECIPE.eb [--source OTHER.eb]... \
  [--overrides OVERRIDES.toml]... \
  [--json]
```

The backend is read from the recipe's `source_urls`: PyPI, GitHub, GitLab,
CRAN, crates.io, or an HTTP directory listing. Every listed version is
printed as kept, or dropped with its reason: a draft, a pre-release, a
yanked release, or the per-package override (an odd-minor development
series, a highest allowed major). eb-stack carries
`data/upstream-overrides.toml`; `--overrides` files apply after it. The
state is `current`, `behind`, `pinned` or `unknown`. `--json` prints one
array with the same rows. GitHub requests send `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GH_TOKEN`
when set.

# Bundle layout

```text
BUNDLE/
  package.plan.json
  package.sbom.cdx.json
  closure.plan.json
  closure.sbom.cdx.json
  build-order.json
  locks/<profile>.lock.json
  easyconfigs/<letter>/<name>/<recipe>.eb
```

`package plan` writes the three closure files whenever `--easyconfigs` is
passed. `package inspect` writes only the plan and planned SBOM.

`package plan` and `package bump` establish the **resolves** claim only when all
requested locks and recipes are written successfully.

See [package bundle reference](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/package-bundles.html.md) for the complete
manifest, planned SBOM, profile-lock, residual, and recipe contract.

# Recipe commands

```bash
eb-stack recipe easyblock NAME
eb-stack recipe easyblock -- -NAME
eb-stack recipe easyblock --charmap

eb-stack recipe templates --export
eb-stack recipe templates --name NAME --version VERSION

eb-stack recipe hierarchy
eb-stack recipe hierarchy --export

eb-stack recipe check \
  --recipe RECIPE.eb \
  --easyconfigs UPSTREAM \
  [--easyconfigs OVERLAY]... \
  [--easyblocks DIR_OR_FILE]... \
  [--require-configopt FLAG]... \
  [--metadata-only] \
  [--verify-sources \
     [--seeded-from ECOSYSTEM \
        [--seeded-source-url URL] \
        [--seeded-git GIT_REMOTE]] \
     [--source-tree DIR]] \
  [--strict]

eb-stack recipe lint RECIPE.eb [RECIPE.eb ...] [--base BEFORE.eb]
eb-stack recipe format RECIPE.eb [RECIPE.eb ...] [--dry-run]
eb-stack recipe format RECIPE.eb --out FORMATTED.eb
```

`recipe easyblock` prints the class EasyBuild derives from a software name
(`EB_` plus the framework character map). `--charmap` prints that map as JSON
instead. A hyphen-leading name is a name, not an option: pass it directly or
after `--`.

`recipe templates --export` prints the constant table and the derived-key
rules. With `--name` and `--version` it prints the values those rules produce
for that pair, using the lowercased name for the forge-account defaults and
`system` for the toolchain. `recipe hierarchy` prints the known fixture
generations as JSON, parent and members, most minimal subtoolchain first.
`--export` prints the whole table: those generations plus the synthetic
GCC-family rule.

`recipe lint` prints JSON with `clean`, `style` (each finding carries
`path`, `line`, `column`, `code`, `severity`, `message`, and, when set,
`info` and `in_review`), `check_contrib`,
and `maintainer_acceptability`. It does not rely on `eb --check-contrib`.
Style codes: E999 (not valid Python; the syntax-tree rules are skipped); the
easyconfigs CI lint F541 (f-string with no placeholder), W605 (invalid escape
sequence), and W291 (trailing whitespace, including inside `description`);
the check-contrib pycodestyle codes E501 (longer than 120) and
E225/E226/E227/E228/E231; the easyconfigs test-suite checks
`EB_PY_NO_USER_SITE`, `EB_SANITY_PATHS_SHAPE`, `EB_LOCAL_VAR_NAMING`,
`EB_REDEFINED_PARAM`, and `EB_CHECKSUM_COUNT`; and the review conventions
`EB_FMT_MISSING_F`, `EB_FSTRING_QUOTE_REUSE`, `EB_TEMPLATE_UNKNOWN` (errors)
and `EB_FMT_PERCENT`, `EB_FMT_CONCAT`, `EB_FMT_TEMPLATE_VAR`,
`EB_SHLIB_HARDCODED`, and `EB_DEP_DUPLICATE` (warnings).
`clean` is false while any error or any in-scope `EB_FMT_*` finding
remains; `error_free` counts errors only. An `EB_FMT_*` finding with
`info` true is outside the review scope (an untouched `%%(...)s`-escaped
entry or, with `--base`, a line unchanged from the base) and does not count.
With `--base` the diff-mode rules also run: `EB_SANITY_ENTRY_REMOVED` and
`EB_EASYBLOCK_CHANGED` (errors), `EB_SANITY_PATHS_REMOVED` (warning), and
`EB_FMT_TEMPLATE_REMOVED`. `EB_FSTRING_ESCAPED_TEMPLATE` and
`EB_DEP_EMPTY_VERSION` are errors. With `--base`, the file
before the edit, it also reports `EB_FMT_TEMPLATE_REMOVED` where a template
was replaced by a Python expression. `f'lib/%(name)s.{SHLIB_EXT}'` is correct
and not flagged. When `eb` is on `PATH`, the command also runs
`eb --check-contrib` and merges those findings (`origin` is
`eb --check-contrib`). A missing `eb` is reported in `check_contrib` and does
not by itself fail the command. Error-severity findings do; warnings do not. `recipe format` only wraps mechanical E501 lines; the other codes stay in
`remaining`.

`recipe check` refuses a recipe that is not valid Python. It prints the
structured dependency result and fails when package
metadata, checksum structure, required configuration flags, or robot
dependencies are invalid. Missing dependencies remain explicit work; the
command does not create placeholder recipes.

`--require-configopt` takes the flag as it appears in `configopts`, dashes
included (`--require-configopt --with-tests`). `--strict` lists every
statement that failed to parse and fails when that list is not empty.
`if`, `for`, `import`, and the other control keywords stay unreported:
that is the tolerant skip, not a parse failure.
`--verify-sources` classifies each source URL and, with `--seeded-from`,
rejects a checksum copied from a different artifact class. `--seeded-source-url`
and `--seeded-git` require `--seeded-from`, which itself requires
`--verify-sources`. `--source-tree` compares the version the unpacked tree
declares with the recipe version.

It also prints `easyblock_resolution`: the class the recipe resolves to
(named, or derived from the software name), the file that defines it, its
bases and its `extra_options` keys. A bundle's own `easyblocks/` directory,
beside the `easyconfigs/` tree the recipe sits in, is searched first. Naming
`--easyblocks` roots, such as an easyblocks checkout, asserts that the set is
complete: a software-specific `EB_` class found in none of them fails the
check with the message EasyBuild would stop on.

`recipe format` only performs deterministic physical-line wrapping. Product
configuration, source selection, checksums, patches, and sanity paths remain
authored content.

# Stack commands

```bash
eb-stack stack solve \
  --easyconfigs TREE [--easyconfigs OVERLAY]... \
  (--stack-policy POLICY.json | --toolchain NAME/VERSION \
   [--root NAME]... [--roots-from-build-list LIST]...) \
  [--baseline-easyconfigs TREE] \
  [--baseline-toolchain-version VERSION] \
  [--baseline-easystack EASYSTACK.yml]... [--baseline-commits-from EB_REPO] \
  [--baseline-also-toolchain NAME/VERSION]... \
  [--filter-deps NAME,NAME...] \
  [--lock-out /tmp/stack.lock.json] \
  [--sbom-out /tmp/stack.cdx.json] \
  [--build-list-out /tmp/build.list] [--build-list-excludes-baseline] \
  [--jenkins-build-list-out /tmp/next.list [--jenkins-flags-from /tmp/previous.list]... \
   [--jenkins-gpu-systems gpu-a,gpu-b] [--jenkins-roots-only]] \
  [--stack-diff-out /tmp/stack.diff.md]

eb-stack stack sbom --lock /tmp/stack.lock.json [--out /tmp/stack.cdx.json]

eb-stack stack order \
  --easyconfigs TREE [--easyconfigs OVERLAY]... \
  --root NAME [--root NAME==VERSION]... \
  [--filter-deps NAME,NAME...] \
  [--out /tmp/build-order.txt] \
  [--oldest] \
  [--easystack-out /tmp/order.yml] \
  [--hashes-out /tmp/hashes.txt]

eb-stack stack easystack \
  --lock /tmp/stack.lock.json \
  [--out stack.yml | --eessi-version 2026.06 --easybuild-version 5.4.1 \
   --generation 2026.1 --out-dir SOFTWARE_LAYER] \
  [--option FILE.eb:OPTION=VALUE]...

eb-stack stack gap \
  --site SITE-MODULES.txt [--site OTHER.txt]... \
  --installed INSTALLED.txt \
  --easyconfigs TREE [--easyconfigs OVERLAY]... \
  --generation 2026.1 \
  [--exclude-file SITE-ONLY.tsv] \
  [--filter-deps NAME,NAME...] \
  --out-dir GAP

eb-stack stack batch \
  (--root FILE.eb... | --roots-file ROOTS.txt) \
  --easyconfigs TREE [--easyconfigs OVERLAY]... \
  [--commit-tree COMMIT=DIR]... \
  --installed INSTALLED.txt [--installed-modulerc MODULERC]... \
  [--open-prs OPEN.json]... [--open-repo EESSI/software-layer] \
  --eessi-version 2026.06 --easybuild-version 5.4.1 --generation 2026.1 \
  [--filter-deps NAME,NAME...] \
  [--size 3] \
  [--easyconfigs-repo ~/src/easybuild-easyconfigs] \
  [--generated-at 2026-10-29T00:00:00Z] \
  [--arch riscv64]... \
  [--unsupported LIST.toml] \
  --out-dir BATCHES

eb-stack stack arch \
  --easystack EASYSTACK.yml [--easystack OTHER.yml]... \
  [--arch riscv64]... \
  [--easyconfigs TREE]... \
  [--installed INSTALLED.txt | --installed riscv64=INSTALLED.txt]... \
  [--additional-arch FILE.yml | --additional-arch riscv64=DIR]... \
  [--unsupported LIST.toml]

eb-stack stack sections \
  tests/jenkins_sections/next.list \
  --from tests/jenkins_sections/previous.list \
  --out /tmp/grouped.list

eb-stack stack from-commit \
  --easystack 20261011-eb-5.4.0-UCX.yml \
  [--easystack OTHER.yml]... \
  [--easybuild-version 5.4.0] \
  [--easyconfigs-repo ~/src/easybuild-easyconfigs] \
  [--easyblocks-repo ~/src/easybuild-easyblocks] \
  [--rewrite] \
  [--json]
```

`stack sbom` reads the easyconfigs the lock names. A runtime dependency
that is also selected is a CycloneDX `dependsOn` edge. A builddependency
is the component property `eb_stack:buildDependsOn`. `stack solve --sbom-out`
writes that same document, checksums included. The MCP tool
`eb_stack_sbom` writes it too. An unreadable path contributes no edge.

`stack solve` is the multi-root EasyBuild stack solver. Package-profile stack
preferences use the TOML schema documented with the package workflow; whole
stack solving uses the JSON `Policy` schema. The policy file is
`--stack-policy`, the same flag `package plan` and `package bump` take.

The baseline is either a previous generation (`--baseline-easyconfigs`, by
default the first `--easyconfigs` tree) or what a set of easystacks installs
(`--baseline-easystack`, repeatable). An easystack baseline is every entry
plus the closure its recipes pin, read from the `--easyconfigs` trees and kept
to the policy toolchain's hierarchy. An entry pinned with `from-commit` is read
from that commit of `--baseline-commits-from` when given, and matched by
filename otherwise. Entries that name no recipe are listed on standard error.
`--baseline-also-toolchain` keeps another family's hierarchy in the baseline,
such as `lfoss/2026.1` beside a `foss/2026.1` solve. `--filter-deps` drops each named dependency before the solve, together
with the subtree under it, using EasyBuild's matching: a bare name,
`name`version`, or `name`[low:high]`. `[` and `]` include a limit, the
opposite bracket excludes it, and an empty side is open. The last spec for
a name wins. Pass EESSI-extend's `EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS` list when solving
against a European Environment for Scientific Software Installations (EESSI) baseline, or the build list carries modules the compat
