- [Run the annual toolchain-generation bump](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../howto/run-annual-bump.html.md)
  for the batch workflow and claim ladder.
- [Bump one recipe](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../howto/bump-recipe.html.md) for the canonical
  `package bump` inputs and bundle.
- [Campaign state and typed findings](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../reference/campaigns.html.md) for
  empirical build classification and ownership.
- [Tutorial](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../tutorial.html.md) for conda-forge eOn plus the QMCPACK
  profile variant.

# From one easystack line to a build set

`eb-stack pr-overlap` lists the modules a pull request would build,
starting from the easystack lines it adds. This page explains
that walk, and how the tool picks a merge order from those lists. Each added line
names one easyconfig. The tool follows the dependencies of that
easyconfig, then theirs, and stops at each installed module. That follow-up is the dependency walk. The closure is every
module the dependency walk reaches. Every reached module that is not
installed goes into the pull request's build set (`to_build` in the
record). When two build sets share a module, building both pull
requests builds that module twice. The second install replaces the
first. Different hooks or settings in the second build leave a
binary the first pull request never tested. The
command writes `overlap.md` for maintainers, one `prs/<N>.toml` record
per pull request, `overlap.toml`, and, with `--merge-order`,
`merge-order.toml`.

Run it before merging two or more European Environment for Scientific
Software Installations (EESSI) software-layer pull requests (PRs) that
edit the same EESSI version and easystack. A scheduled CI job can run
the same check and publish `overlap.md`. The commands and the CI wiring are in
[find shared builds across open pull requests](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../howto/pr-overlap.html.md).
Record fields are in [output formats](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../reference/formats.html.md).

# One shared module

`tests/pr_overlap_fixtures/` has three pull requests. Pull requests 11
and 13 both add `freetype-2.14.1-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb`. Pull request 12
adds `Graphviz-14.0.2-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb`, and Graphviz depends on
freetype. The installed list is `GCCcore/15.2.0`,
`zlib/1.3.1-GCCcore-15.2.0`, and `CMake/4.1.2-GCCcore-15.2.0`.

```bash
eb-stack pr-overlap \
  --pr tests/pr_overlap_fixtures/prs.json \
  --easyconfigs tests/pr_overlap_fixtures/release \
  --installed tests/pr_overlap_fixtures/installed.txt \
  --installed-label x86_64/amd/zen4 \
  --generated-at 2026-10-22T00:00:00Z \
  --merge-order \
  --out-dir /tmp/pr-overlap-explain
```

The command prints one line:

```
prs=3 records=3 shared_modules=2 skipped_easyconfigs=0 out=/tmp/pr-overlap-explain
```

`prs` is the number of distinct pull requests read. `records` is the
number that add at least one entry to an easystack selected for this
stack version and architecture. `shared_modules` is the number of
not-yet-installed module names present in more than one record's
`to_build` list. `skipped_easyconfigs` is the number of recipe files
skipped while loading the easyconfig trees because the parser could not
parse them. `out` is the directory containing `overlap.md`,
`overlap.toml`, the per-PR records, and `merge-order.toml`.

`/tmp/pr-overlap-explain/overlap.md` names the two shared modules:
`freetype/2.14.1-GCCcore-15.2.0` and `libpng/1.6.50-GCCcore-15.2.0`,
each on pull requests 11, 12, and 13. Merge pull request 11 first.
After that, pull request 13 has nothing left to build, and pull request
12 builds only Graphviz.
[[*How merge order changes later builds][How merge order changes later builds]]
is why 11 is first.

# From one line to a build set

The base easystack already contains zlib. Pull request 11 adds
freetype:

```diff
 easyconfigs:
   - zlib-1.3.1-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb
+  - freetype-2.14.1-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb
```

Lines already on the base are not new work. The tool resolves each
added filename on `--easyconfigs`, then follows dependencies. A module
name has the form `name/version[-toolchain]versionsuffix`. The
toolchain part is absent for a recipe built with the system toolchain.
`freetype-2.14.1-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb` asks for
`freetype/2.14.1-GCCcore-15.2.0`.

The diagram below summarizes pull request 12's dependency walk.
It is explanatory, not text printed by the command:

```text
Graphviz/14.0.2-GCCcore-15.2.0                 to build (PR 12)
├── freetype/2.14.1-GCCcore-15.2.0             to build (PRs 11, 12, 13)
│   ├── libpng/1.6.50-GCCcore-15.2.0           to build
│   │   ├── zlib/1.3.1-GCCcore-15.2.0          installed, stop
│   │   └── CMake/4.1.2-GCCcore-15.2.0         installed, stop
│   └── zlib/1.3.1-GCCcore-15.2.0              installed, stop
└── libpng/1.6.50-GCCcore-15.2.0               same module
toolchain GCCcore/15.2.0                       installed, stop
```

`to_build` for pull request 12 is Graphviz, freetype, and libpng.
`already_installed` is CMake, GCCcore, and zlib. Pull requests 11 and
13 start at freetype, so they build freetype and libpng.

When the dependency walk reaches an installed module, it records that
module and stops following its dependencies. Copy the installed list,
add `freetype/2.14.1-GCCcore-15.2.0`, and pass that file as
`--installed`. The summary then has `shared_modules=0`. Pull requests
11 and 13 have an empty build set. Pull request 12 still builds
Graphviz and libpng, because it names libpng itself, and lists freetype
as installed.

# Where the dependency walk stops

`--filter-deps` drops dependency tuples before the walk starts. EasyBuild's
`--filter-deps` does the same. A name drops every version and
every module reached only through it. Omit the flag and the command
reads `EASYBUILD_FILTER_DEPS` when that variable is set. On this
fixture, `--filter-deps libpng` drops libpng from the build set of pull
request 12. Graphviz and freetype stay, and `shared_modules` is 1.
CMake leaves `already_installed`, because the dependency walk reached
it only through libpng.

# An alias counts as the installed module

Pass `--installed-modulerc` with an Lmod `.modulerc.lua` file, or with
a `modules/all` tree. `module_version("Java/21.0.8", "21")` adds
`Java/21` to the installed set when `Java/21.0.8` is already on the
list, and a dependency on `Java/21` stops there. Without the modulerc,
`Java/21` stays in the build set.

# A missing easyblock is unresolved

A recipe that sets no `easyblock` takes the class EasyBuild derives
from its name, so `eOn` becomes `EB_eOn`. Pass `--easyblocks` with the
installed `easybuild/easyblocks` package. A missing class is recorded
as `easyblock EB_eOn missing` in `unresolved`. That module is left out
of the build set. Its dependencies stay. `overlap.md` prints
`- unresolved: easyblock EB_eOn missing`.

`include-easyblocks-from-commit` names a commit. Pass those files as
`--easyblocks-commit COMMIT=DIR`. When the class is in that tree, the
module stays in the build set and the record notes where it came from.
A commit you did not pass stays unresolved, with a note that it was not
provided. Treat an unresolved easyblock as an incomplete result. Supply
the installed easyblocks package with `--easyblocks`, or the requested
commit files with `--easyblocks-commit`, and rerun the command before
choosing a merge order.

# How merge order changes later builds

`--merge-order` writes `merge-order.toml` and appends a table to
`overlap.md`. The proposed order takes every module of an earlier step
as installed before the next step starts. On that basis, shared modules are assigned only to
their first step:

1. A pull request that adds a module to the easystack by name goes
   before any pull request that only reaches that module as a
   dependency. Two pull requests that both add it by name have no order
   between them. A `depends-on` row works the same way.
2. Of the pull requests that nothing else has to precede, take the one
   with the fewest modules left to build. On a tie, take the lowest
   number.
3. Count the modules of that pull request as installed. Recount the
   modules left for each remaining pull request. `saves` records what
   each one lost.
4. If pull requests must each go before the other, the report lists
   that cycle under `cycles`. The tool then ignores requirements within
   the cycle and applies rule 2. Review the cycle before merging,
   because no ordering can satisfy all of its internal requirements.

On the fixture, pull requests 11 and 13 both ask for freetype. Neither
has to precede the other. Each must precede pull request 12,
because 12 only reaches freetype. Both have 2 modules left to build, so
the lower number wins. The first step in
`/tmp/pr-overlap-explain/merge-order.toml` is:

```text
[[steps]]
position = 1
pr = 11
after = []
builds = ["freetype/2.14.1-GCCcore-15.2.0", "libpng/1.6.50-GCCcore-15.2.0"]
reason = "smallest residual build set (2)"
```

The word "residual" in `reason` is the modules left to build. That step
records freetype and libpng in `saves` for pull requests 12 and 13.
Position 2 is pull request 13, which has no modules left to build.
Position 3 is pull request 12, which still builds Graphviz, and its
`after` lists 11 and 13.

`--merged` numbers are not steps. Their build sets count as installed
before rule 2. `--impact N` treats only N's build set as newly
installed. `--impact 11` shrinks pull requests 12 and 13 by freetype
and libpng, and the freetype row resolves for 12 only, because 13 asks
for freetype itself. A number outside the input exits 2 and names it:
`--merged 999: no pull request with that number`.

An easyconfigs pull request has no easystack entries, so rule 1 reads
its `depends-on` rows instead. Each row runs from pull request A to pull
request B and has one of two causes. In the first, A adds a module. B's
closure needs that module, and B does not add it. In the second, A edits
or deletes an easyconfig, and B builds a dependent of that module
without changing it. B builds a dependent when the module is in B's
closure, or when B's `to_build` lists one of A's reverse dependents. The
edited easyconfig joins A's `to_build` because A edits it. The rebuild
classes apply to A's reverse dependents. A bundle whose `exts_list`
names that package is `must-rebuild`, and it joins A's `to_build` even
when the bundle is already installed. A runtime dependent is
`no-rebuild`, and a dependent reached only through builddependencies is
`review`. Both are listed under reverse dependents with depth and class,
and neither is scheduled. A toolchain edge is not listed. `--impact A`
lists the edited module under `resolves` for B.

`merge-order.toml` and the last table in `overlap.md` also list
easystack edits that will collide in git. `same-entry` means two pull
requests add the identical line. `same-insertion` means they add lines
at the same place in the same easystack. Open those PR diffs before
merging: identical entries are likely duplicates, while additions at
the same location may cause a textual merge conflict. Here pull
requests 11 and 13 are `same-entry`, and all three are
`same-insertion`. The place is found by a line diff of base and head.
`revisions` in each record keeps the text that check was computed from.

# Every entry of a changed easystack

The sections above walk the lines a pull request adds. The EESSI bot
builds a larger set. The bot for one architecture reads each changed
easystack at the pull request head. The bot then builds every entry in that file
not yet installed there, plus the missing dependencies of those
entries. An entry an earlier pull request added stays
in the file. If one architecture never installed it, every later pull
request that touches the file builds it again on that architecture.

Software-layer pull request 1775 added lines to
`eessi-2026.06-eb-5.4.0-2026.1.yml`. GDRCopy was already in that file,
and the riscv64 bot failed on it. The added-lines walk does not reach
GDRCopy, because 1775 did not add it. x86_64 had GDRCopy installed, so
the whole-file walk on x86_64 does not build it either.

`--arch-installed` runs the whole-file walk once per architecture and
gives each architecture its own build set, merge order, and impact.
`entries` in the record stays the lines the pull request added. A head
entry that was already in the file and is still not installed is
listed as `carried`. The command and its output are in
[find shared builds across open pull requests](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../howto/pr-overlap.html.md).

# What to do with the report

1. Open `overlap.md` and investigate every `unresolved` item and any
   nonzero `skipped_easyconfigs` count. Either can make a build set
   incomplete.
2. Process the first unmerged step in `merge-order.toml` through the
   normal EESSI merge, build, and publication workflow.
3. Refresh the installed-module list and rerun `pr-overlap` before
   acting on the next step.

The report is a prediction from recipe metadata and the supplied
installed-module list. It is not evidence that a recipe resolves in
EasyBuild, builds successfully, or produces a verified binary.

# What an in-place patch forces a rebuild of

The patch keeps the easyconfig filename and the version. ~eb-stack
rebuild-set~ closes the deployed easystacks and walks backward from each
patched easyconfig through the installed modules. The closure is everything
that depends on the patched module within its toolchain generation. An
unpinned dependency is resolved inside the dependent's own generation, so
a module built with another generation is not a row.

The walk starts from the easyconfig graph. `--prefix` and `--check-static`
then read the installed files. The commands are in
[what an in-place patch forces the European Environment for Scientific Software Installations (EESSI) to rebuild](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../howto/rebuild-set.html.md).
The output fields are in [output formats](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../reference/formats.html.md).

# Three classes

- `no-rebuild`. Some path from the patched module is made of runtime
  dependencies. The dependent links the patched package as a shared
  library. Replacing that library does not require a rebuild.
- `review`. Every path uses a builddependency. The dependent may have
  linked the package statically or embedded it. The graph cannot say
  which, and the reason says so.
- `must-rebuild`. The row is the patched easyconfig, or a bundle whose
  `exts_list` names that package and version. The extension is installed
  as part of the bundle.

The strongest class wins: must-rebuild, then review, then no-rebuild. A
runtime path beats a builddependency path, so a module listed in both
`dependencies` and `builddependencies` is no-rebuild.

An extension makes that bundle must-rebuild. It does not force the same
class on modules that depend on the bundle. Those modules are classified
by their own edges. A runtime dependency on the bundle is no-rebuild, and
the reason names the bundle.

A toolchain edge is indexed and not classified. Patching a compiler is
outside these three classes.

A review dependent is reported once. The changed column lists every
patched easyconfig that put it there. When `--prefix` found static
archives, the reason names them. The other classes stay one row per edge.

# Installed archives

`--prefix` is the installed prefix of EESSI. The install directory of
`Name/version` is `software/Name/version`. A static archive is a `*.a`
file directly under a `lib*` directory there.

A patched module whose directory exists and contains no such file cannot
have been linked statically. A builddependency-only dependent of that
module is no-rebuild, and the reason is `no static archive installed`.
Archives that are there keep the row in review, and the reason names
them. A missing install directory is a note. The row stays in review. A
prefix with no `software` directory is an error.

# Defined symbols

`--check-static` is off unless it is passed, and it needs `--prefix`. It
reads defined dynamic symbols of each remaining review dependent and
compares them with the exports of the patched libraries that put the row
in review. The exports come from `lib**/**.so` and `lib**/**.so.*`, skipping
symlinks. When that set is empty, they come from the global and weak
defined symbols in the `*.a` members. Version suffixes (`@@VERS` and
`@VERS`) are stripped before the comparison.

A hit means the dependent defines an export of the patched library, which
is what a static link copies in. The row becomes must-rebuild, and the
reason names the file and the symbols. No hit, and a readable export set,
is no-rebuild. An empty export set stays in review. A missing install
directory of the dependent is a note, and the row stays in review.

The scan can go wrong. It sees dynamic symbols only, so a hidden, local,
or inlined static link is a false no-rebuild. A short name shared with
another library is a false must-rebuild. Scripts, bytecode, and libraries
opened with dlopen are invisible. A static archive shows that a static
link was possible, not that it happened.

# What counts as installed

The reverse walk visits installed modules only. It does not continue
through a module that is not installed, so a dependent that is reachable
only through an uninstalled intermediate is left out. The patched
easyconfig itself is must-rebuild when it is in the deployed graph, even
when that module is not installed.

`--filter-deps` drops `dependencies` and `builddependencies` tuples before
the walk. It leaves `exts_list` in place. A filtered package that a bundle
includes as an extension still marks that bundle must-rebuild.

A missing easyblock class is a note. The module stays in the set, because
it is already installed. A `from-commit` whose tree was not passed is a
note, and the release tree is used for that pin.

# Scanner findings

`--findings` turns a scanner export into the changed list: every installed
module it names. The rebuild set is then read twice per module. A
backported patch that keeps the version replaces files under the same
module path, so the cost is the must-rebuild and review rows. A new
version is a new path. EasyBuild writes each dependency version into the
dependent's module file and run path, so the cost is the module and every
installed dependent, runtime and builddependency alike. The ratio between
the two is the case for backports over bumps, per module.

A site that installs from build lists has no easystack. Without
`--easystack`, the installed list is the stack: each module is read as the
easyconfig its name gives, and a module that no easyconfig matches is
listed as unresolved.

# Example

Patch `zlib-1.3.1-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb`. `libpng` depends on zlib, so libpng
is no-rebuild. `Graphviz` depends on libpng, so Graphviz is no-rebuild
through libpng. `CMake` lists zlib only as a builddependency, so CMake is
review. A bundle whose `exts_list` names zlib 1.3.1 is must-rebuild. An
application that depends on that bundle at runtime is no-rebuild.

The rebuild easystack contains zlib and the bundle, each with
`rebuild: true`. It does not contain libpng.

With `--prefix`, the CMake row stays in review only when the installed
zlib provides a static archive, and the reason names that archive. With
`--check-static`, CMake is must-rebuild when one of its installed Executable and Linkable Format (ELF)
files defines an export of that archive, and no-rebuild when none of
them does.

# Dependency closure

A dependency closure lists every module one change reaches. The change
may be an easyconfig, an easyblock, or one bundled component. A software
bill of materials (SBOM) records the components and the edges. The record
is planned: the recipes supply it before anything is installed.

An easyconfig author reads the closure of one recipe bump. A reviewer
compares pull requests that share a file or a module. An easyblock author
lists the recipes that name a changed class. A framework author lists
those recipes. Triage lists the installed modules that carry one component
from a Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) entry. A software-layer
maintainer lists the pull requests that would build one module. A site
maintainer lists the installed modules an upstream pull request changes.
The annual toolchain bump is the generation step in the first section. A
security or compliance reader consumes the CycloneDX document. A
conda-forge porter reads the planned SBOM from `package inspect`. A Spack
porter reads that document too.

The runs below use recorded slices of upstream trees.
`tests/sbom_recorded/cbc`, `tests/sbom_recorded/gromacs`,
`tests/sbom_recorded/quarto`, and `tests/sbom_recorded/rebuild` are byte
copies of easybuild-easyconfigs `develop` at
`981d2123dddccca9ce0b15f9eb2643e872332f5e`, the commit
`scripts/fetch-upstream-trees.sh` creates a checkout of. The easyconfigs under
`tests/pr_overlap_layer` are the same kind of copy. `prs.json` there is
the recorded pull-request file for software-layer pull requests 1585 and 1728.
`tests/sbom_recorded/easyblock` is a byte copy of the v5.4.1 easyblocks,
framework, and easyconfigs tags that script pins.
`tests/sbom_recorded/foreign` is the conda-forge zlib feedstock recipe at
`e34000ac354055f133215d211048bc3289afe5f4` and the Spack zlib `package.py`
at `a19611deab3c33e3b2855b8379e8ddee12ef843a`. Each directory keeps the
upstream licence file. `tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open` is the recorded
open easybuild-easyconfigs pull requests.
`tests/component_reach_recorded` is the cURL and git slice from the same
develop commit. The runs write under `/tmp/sbom-demo`.

```bash
eb-stack --version
```

```text
eb-stack 0.3.0
```

The how-tos name the flags for each command:
[pull-request overlap](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../howto/pr-overlap.html.md),
[an in-place patch](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../howto/rebuild-set.html.md),
[a named component](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../howto/component-reach.html.md),
[an easyblock change](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../howto/easyblock-reach.html.md), and
[a recipe bump](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../howto/bump-recipe.html.md). Output fields are in
[output formats](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../reference/formats.html.md).

# The annual toolchain bump

A generation maintainer asks which packages change version together.
The recorded step is foss-2025a to foss-2025b for Cbc. The slice has the
foss-2025b closure of `Cbc-2.10.12` and the foss-2025a counterparts of
Cbc, Cgl, Clp, and MUMPS. `stack solve --sbom-out` writes a CycloneDX 1.5
document for the selection. `stack sbom --lock` writes the same document
later, from the lock. Both commands read edges and checksums from the
easyconfigs the lock names. A runtime dependency that is also selected is
a `dependsOn` edge. A builddependency is the component property
`eb_stack:buildDependsOn`. The document does not draw an edge from every
package to every other package.

`--build-list-out` writes the easyconfigs to build.
`--jenkins-roots-only` writes one Jenkins line for the policy root and
leaves the dependencies to `eb --robot`.

```bash
eb-stack stack solve \
  --easyconfigs tests/sbom_recorded/cbc \
  --baseline-easyconfigs tests/sbom_recorded/cbc \
  --toolchain foss/2025b \
  --root Cbc \
  --lock-out /tmp/sbom-demo/stack.lock.json \
  --sbom-out /tmp/sbom-demo/stack.cdx.json \
  --stack-diff-out /tmp/sbom-demo/stack.diff.md \
  --build-list-out /tmp/sbom-demo/build.list \
  --jenkins-build-list-out /tmp/sbom-demo/jenkins.list \
  --jenkins-roots-only
```

```text
lock=/tmp/sbom-demo/stack.lock.json packages=58
```

```bash
cat /tmp/sbom-demo/build.list
```

# A CycloneDX consumer

A scanner identifies these components by package URL. The type is
`pkg:generic`. The document carries no Common Platform Enumeration (CPE)
identity. `compositions[0].aggregate` is `complete` when the solve named
every dependency.

```bash
echo aggregate=$(jq -r '.compositions[0].aggregate' /tmp/sbom-demo/stack.cdx.json)
echo purl=$(jq -r '.components[] | select(.name=="Cbc") | .purl' /tmp/sbom-demo/stack.cdx.json)
echo cpe=$(jq -r '[.components[] | .cpe // empty] | length' /tmp/sbom-demo/stack.cdx.json)
```

```text
aggregate=complete
purl=pkg:generic/Cbc@2.10.12?toolchain=foss-2025b
cpe=0
```

# A conda-forge or Spack porter

`package inspect` writes the planned SBOM for one foreign recipe. The
conda-forge file is `recipe/meta.yaml` from `conda-forge/zlib-feedstock`
at `e34000ac354055f133215d211048bc3289afe5f4`. The package name in that
recipe is `zlib-split` and the version is 1.3.2. The Spack file is
`package.py` from `spack/spack-packages` at
`a19611deab3c33e3b2855b8379e8ddee12ef843a`. The licence texts sit next to
the recipes. A build-only dependency is `eb_stack:buildDependsOn`. It is
absent from `dependsOn`. The package-plan document kind stays
`eb-stack:document-kind`, value `canonical-package-plan`.

eb-stack package inspect \

  --out-dir /tmp/sbom-demo/conda

# A checksum dict when the version changes

The hash in that SBOM has to name the artifact the new version will fetch.
`quarto-1.8.26.eb` on develop uses the SYSTEM toolchain. `local_archs`
sends `aarch64` to `arm64` and `x86_64` to `amd64`. `sources` indexes that
map with `ARCH`. The checksum dict has an `amd64` key and an `arm64` key.
A version bump passes one digest on `--source-checksum`.

```bash
eb-stack package bump \
  --source tests/sbom_recorded/quarto/easybuild/easyconfigs/q/quarto/quarto-1.8.26.eb \
  --toolchain system \
  --version 1.8.27 \
  --source-checksum dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd \
  --easyconfigs tests/sbom_recorded/quarto \
  --out-dir /tmp/sbom-demo/ck/out
```

```text
manifest=/tmp/sbom-demo/ck/out/package.plan.json
sbom=/tmp/sbom-demo/ck/out/package.sbom.cdx.json
lock=/tmp/sbom-demo/ck/out/locks/default.lock.json
easyconfig=/tmp/sbom-demo/ck/out/easyconfigs/q/quarto/quarto-1.8.27.eb
```

```bash
cat /tmp/sbom-demo/ck/out/easyconfigs/q/quarto/quarto-1.8.27.eb
```

```text
easyblock = 'Tarball'

name = 'quarto'
version = '1.8.27'

homepage = 'https://quarto.org/'
description = '''
    An open-source scientific and technical publishing system.
'''

toolchain = SYSTEM

source_urls = ['https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/download/v%(version)s/']
local_archs = {'aarch64': 'arm64', 'x86_64': 'amd64'}
sources = ['quarto-%%(version)s-linux-%s.tar.gz' % local_archs[ARCH]]

checksums = [{
    'quarto-%(version)s-linux-amd64.tar.gz': 'dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd',
    'quarto-%(version)s-linux-arm64.tar.gz': '',
}]

modextrapaths = {'PATH': ''}

sanity_check_paths = {
    'files': ['bin/quarto'],
    'dirs': []
}

sanity_check_commands = ["quarto check"]

moduleclass = 'devel'
```

The expression key is renamed to 1.8.27 and receives the digest from
`--source-checksum`. The arm64 key is renamed and left empty. The easyblock
stays `Tarball`. The SBOM root hash is the digest that was passed in.

```bash
jq -r '.metadata.component.hashes[0] | "\(.alg) \(.content)"' /tmp/sbom-demo/ck/out/package.sbom.cdx.json
```

```text
SHA-256 dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd
```

```bash
jq '.components | length' /tmp/sbom-demo/ck/out/package.sbom.cdx.json
```

```text
1
```

`recipe lint` reports the doubled percent sign that the recipe uses so a
later `%` expansion leaves one percent. `recipe check` resolves the
metadata and counts both checksum slots.

```bash
eb-stack recipe lint /tmp/sbom-demo/ck/out/easyconfigs/q/quarto/quarto-1.8.27.eb | jq -c '{clean, error_free, codes: [.style[].code]}'
```

```text
{"clean":true,"error_free":true,"codes":["EB_FMT_PERCENT"]}
```

```bash
eb-stack recipe check \
  --recipe /tmp/sbom-demo/ck/out/easyconfigs/q/quarto/quarto-1.8.27.eb \
  --easyconfigs tests/sbom_recorded/quarto
```

    "name": "system",

recipe resolves

# Pull requests

A software-layer maintainer wants the shared modules. The recorded pair is
pull requests 1585 and 1728 on `EESSI/software-layer` at
`b2c10c7278f8b741f4053ddb2907dc4d062063d1`. Both change
`easystacks/software.eessi.io/2026.06/eessi-2026.06-eb-5.4.0-2026.1.yml`.
1585 adds `SciPy-bundle-2026.05-gfbf-2026.1.eb`. 1728 adds
`PLUMED-2.10.0-foss-2026.1.eb`, and that recipe depends on SciPy-bundle
2026.05. The JSON in `tests/pr_overlap_layer/prs.json` is the base and
head text of that easystack for each pull request. The easyconfigs tree
is the 109 modules the two closures reach, copied from
develop `981d2123dddccca9ce0b15f9eb2643e872332f5e`. The installed list is a
comment, because this checkout has no mounted prefix. `--installed` is
still required for the software-layer kind.
`prs/<N>.toml` is the build set for pull request N. `overlap.toml` and
`overlap.md` are the intersection.

The 1585/1728 pair is a replay of a recorded state. Pull request 1585
merged on 2026-09-04. The recorded base of 1728 already lists
`SciPy-bundle-2026.05-gfbf-2026.1.eb`. The two used different bases.
The command replays 1728's easystack against an empty `installed.txt`,
which is why the pair shares 91 modules.

To run it on live pull requests, clone `EESSI/software-layer` and write
one JSON file per open pull request with
`examples/eessi-pr-overlap/fetch-prs.sh`. Pass those files as repeated
`--pr` arguments, and pass the prefix's installed module list as
`--installed`. [The how-to](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../howto/pr-overlap.html.md) gives the
commands under "Run it on a mounted stack".

The software-layer kind keeps an easystack whose path contains
`--eessi-version`. The default is 2026.06. The easyconfigs kind ignores
the flag.

```bash
eb-stack pr-overlap \
  --pr tests/pr_overlap_layer/prs.json \
  --easyconfigs tests/pr_overlap_layer \
  --installed tests/pr_overlap_layer/installed.txt \
  --installed-label none \
  --generated-at 2026-10-24T00:00:00Z \
  --repo-url https://github.com/EESSI/software-layer \
  --eessi-version 2026.06 \
  --out-dir /tmp/sbom-demo/pr/out
```

```text
prs=2 records=2 shared_modules=91 skipped_easyconfigs=0 out=/tmp/sbom-demo/pr/out
```

```bash
sed -n '1,8p' /tmp/sbom-demo/pr/out/prs/1585.toml
```

```text
# Generated by `eb-stack pr-overlap`. Data only: the branch holding this file is
# regenerated on every run and must never be merged.

schema_version = 1
pr = 1585
head_sha = "5abcffa10e4d63a6494f51340474a2f95502adf2"
title = "Merge pull request #1585 from bedroge/2026.1_scipy_bundle"
generated_at = "2026-10-24T00:00:00Z"
```

The generated-file header comes first. `schema_version = 1` follows it.
This is the software-layer schema. The title is the merge subject of pull
request 1585. `overlap.md` has one row per shared module. The SciPy-bundle
row names both pull requests:

```bash
grep -F '| `SciPy-bundle/2026.05-gfbf-2026.1` |' /tmp/sbom-demo/pr/out/overlap.md
```

```text
| `SciPy-bundle/2026.05-gfbf-2026.1` | [#1585](https://github.com/EESSI/software-layer/pull/1585), [#1728](https://github.com/EESSI/software-layer/pull/1728) |
```

`--merge-order` writes `merge-order.toml`. The extract below drops the
non-empty `builds` and `modules` arrays. The reason on position 1 is the
tool's own count.

```bash
eb-stack pr-overlap \
  --pr tests/pr_overlap_layer/prs.json \
  --easyconfigs tests/pr_overlap_layer \
  --installed tests/pr_overlap_layer/installed.txt \
  --installed-label none \
  --generated-at 2026-10-24T00:00:00Z \
  --repo-url https://github.com/EESSI/software-layer \
  --eessi-version 2026.06 \
  --merge-order \
  --out-dir /tmp/sbom-demo/pr/order
```

```text
prs=2 records=2 shared_modules=91 skipped_easyconfigs=0 out=/tmp/sbom-demo/pr/order
```

```bash
python3 - << 'PY'
from pathlib import Path
for line in Path("/tmp/sbom-demo/pr/order/merge-order.toml").read_text().splitlines():
    if line.startswith(("builds = [", "modules = [")) and "[]" not in line:
        continue
    print(line)
PY
```

```text
# Generated by `eb-stack pr-overlap`. Data only: the branch holding this file is
# regenerated on every run and must never be merged.

schema_version = 1
generated_at = "2026-10-24T00:00:00Z"
installed_source = "none"
merged = []
cycles = []
conflicts = []

[[steps]]
position = 1
pr = 1585
after = []
reason = "smallest residual build set (91)"

[[steps.saves]]
pr = 1728

[[steps]]
position = 2
pr = 1728
after = [1585]
saves = []
reason = "smallest residual build set (18)"
```

Position 1 is pull request 1585. Its `builds` array has 91 modules and
`after` is empty. Position 2 is pull request 1728. Its `builds` array has
18 modules and `after` is 1585. The same order run is what
[the how-to](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/../howto/pr-overlap.html.md) quotes.

The easyconfigs kind does not need an installed list. The recorded open
pull requests are `tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open`, closed against the
same develop commit on 2026-10-24. An easyconfigs record uses
`schema_version = 2`, still after the generated-file header.

```bash
eb-stack pr-overlap --kind easyconfigs \
  --pr tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/prs.json \
  --easyconfigs tests/pr_overlap_easyconfigs_open/tree \
  --generated-at 2026-10-24T00:00:00Z \
  --repo-url https://github.com/easybuilders/easybuild-easyconfigs \
  --out-dir /tmp/sbom-demo/ec/out
```

```text
prs=4 records=4 shared_modules=1 skipped_easyconfigs=0 out=/tmp/sbom-demo/ec/out
```

```bash
sed -n '1,6p' /tmp/sbom-demo/ec/out/prs/22823.toml
```

# Generated by `eb-stack pr-overlap`. Data only: the branch holding this file is
# regenerated on every run and must never be merged.

the same file are in

# An in-place patch

A patch can keep the easyconfig filename and the version. The rebuild
class of an installed module still changes. `rebuild-set` closes the
deployed easystacks and walks backward. The recorded inputs are the 90
easyconfigs named by `eessi-2026.06-eb-5.4.0-2026.1.yml` in the software
layer, copied from the same develop commit, with `git-2.52.0-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb`
as the changed file and `git/2.52.0-GCCcore-15.2.0` as the installed module.

```bash
eb-stack rebuild-set \
  --easyconfigs tests/sbom_recorded/rebuild \
  --installed tests/sbom_recorded/rebuild/installed.txt \
  --installed-label none \
  --generated-at 2026-10-24T00:00:00Z \
  --changed tests/sbom_recorded/rebuild/changed.txt \
  --easystack tests/sbom_recorded/rebuild/easystacks/eessi-2026.06-eb-5.4.0-2026.1.yml \
  --out-dir /tmp/sbom-demo/rebuild
```

```text
changed=1 rows=1 must-rebuild=1 review=0 no-rebuild=0 missing=0 easystacks=1 skipped_easyconfigs=0 out=/tmp/sbom-demo/rebuild
```

```bash
python3 - << 'PY'
from pathlib import Path
text = Path("/tmp/sbom-demo/rebuild/rebuild-set.md").read_text()
for line in text.splitlines():
    if line.startswith("Classes follow"):
        print(line.split(". ", 1)[0] + ".")
    if line.startswith("`--check-static` was not used"):
        print(line.split(". ", 1)[0] + ".")
PY
```

```text
Classes follow the easyconfig graph only.
`--check-static` was not used.
```

```bash
sed -n '27,29p' /tmp/sbom-demo/rebuild/rebuild-set.md
```

```text
| Changed easyconfig | Dependent | Edge kind | Class | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `git-2.52.0-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb` | `git/2.52.0-GCCcore-15.2.0` | changed | must-rebuild | patched easyconfig |
```

The report has one row: the changed git easyconfig, class must-rebuild.
The easystack entries do not depend on that git module, so the walk does
not add a second row. The report also notes each `from-commit` pin whose
tree was not passed and says the release tree was used for that pin.
`--check-static` was not passed, and the report says so. Classes follow
the easyconfig graph only.

# A component named by a CVE

The CVE names a component and a version. `component-reach` lists every
recipe in one toolchain generation that carries that component, then feeds
the recipes that contain the bytes into the same rebuild closure. The
recorded tree is `tests/component_reach_recorded`: `cURL-8.17.0-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb`
and `git-2.52.0-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb` from the same develop commit. The name
match ignores letter case and requires a whole token, so `curl` selects
the recipe named `cURL`.

```bash
eb-stack component-reach \
  --component curl \
  --version '>=8,<9' \
  --generation 2026.1 \
  --easyconfigs tests/component_reach_recorded \
  --generated-at 2026-10-24T00:00:00Z \
  --out-dir /tmp/sbom-demo/component-curl
```

```text
component=curl version=>=8,<9 generation=2026.1 carriers=2 changed=1 must-rebuild=1 review=0 no-rebuild=1 out=/tmp/sbom-demo/component-curl
```

```bash
sed -n '5,16p' /tmp/sbom-demo/component-curl/component-reach.md
```

```text
2 carriers. Closure: 1 must-rebuild, 0 review, 1 no-rebuild.

| Easyconfig | Module | Role | Version | Installed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cURL-8.17.0-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb` | `cURL/8.17.0-GCCcore-15.2.0` | module | 8.17.0 | - |
| `git-2.52.0-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb` | `git/2.52.0-GCCcore-15.2.0` | dependency | 8.17.0 | - |

| Changed easyconfig | Dependent | Edge kind | Class | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cURL-8.17.0-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb` | `cURL/8.17.0-GCCcore-15.2.0` | changed | must-rebuild | patched easyconfig |
| `cURL-8.17.0-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb` | `git/2.52.0-GCCcore-15.2.0` | runtime | no-rebuild | runtime dependency; links the patched package as a shared library |
```

`carriers=2` is the cURL module and git as a dependency on cURL 8.17.0.
The closure rebuilds cURL and classifies git as no-rebuild. That slice has
no `libcurl` recipe and no `curl-config` recipe.

# An easyblock or a framework class

An easyblock change reaches the recipes that name that class, a subclass,
or the implied `EB_<Name>` class. `--reverse` then lists modules that
depend on a hit and are not themselves hits. The recorded files are from
the v5.4.1 tags. `easybuild/framework/easyblock.py` defines `EasyBlock`.
`configuremake.py` defines `ConfigureMake(EasyBlock)`.
`cmakemake.py` defines `CMakeMake(ConfigureMake)`. `g/gromacs.py` defines
`EB_GROMACS(CMakeMake)`. The easyconfigs are `zfp-1.0.1-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb`
(`easyblock = 'CMakeMake'`), `make-4.4.1-GCCcore-15.2.0.eb`
(`ConfigureMake`), `GROMACS-2024.4-foss-2024a.eb` (no `easyblock` line),
and `ADIOS2-2.10.2-foss-2025b.eb` (`CMakeMake`, and it depends on
`('zfp', '1.0.1')`). The installed list names `zfp/1.0.1-GCCcore-15.2.0`.

```bash
eb-stack easyblock-reach \
  --easyblocks tests/sbom_recorded/easyblock/easyblocks \
  --framework tests/sbom_recorded/easyblock/framework \
  --easyconfigs tests/sbom_recorded/easyblock/easyconfigs \
  --file tests/sbom_recorded/easyblock/easyblocks/easybuild/easyblocks/generic/cmakemake.py \
  --installed tests/sbom_recorded/easyblock/installed.txt \
  --reverse \
  --generated-at 2026-10-24T00:00:00Z \
  --out-dir /tmp/sbom-demo/ebreach/cmake
```

```text
easyconfigs=3 installed=1 classes=2 reverse=0 out=/tmp/sbom-demo/ebreach/cmake
```

```bash
sed -n '12,26p' /tmp/sbom-demo/ebreach/cmake/reach.md
```

```text
Changed: CMakeMake, EB_GROMACS.

Reached: CMakeMake, EB_GROMACS.

## Easyconfigs

| Module | Class | Via | Detail | Installed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ADIOS2/2.10.2-foss-2025b` | `CMakeMake` | easyblock |  | no |
| `GROMACS/2024.4-foss-2024a` | `EB_GROMACS` | implied |  | no |
| `zfp/1.0.1-GCCcore-15.2.0` | `CMakeMake` | easyblock |  | yes |

## Rebuild

None.
```

Changing `cmakemake.py` reaches `CMakeMake` and `EB_GROMACS`. The three
easyconfigs are ADIOS2, GROMACS, and zfp. `make` is absent, because
`ConfigureMake` was not the change. `reverse=0`: ADIOS2 depends on zfp and
is itself a `CMakeMake` hit, so it is already in the easyconfig table.
The rebuild section is empty.

```bash
eb-stack easyblock-reach \
  --easyblocks tests/sbom_recorded/easyblock/easyblocks \
  --framework tests/sbom_recorded/easyblock/framework \
  --easyconfigs tests/sbom_recorded/easyblock/easyconfigs \
  --file tests/sbom_recorded/easyblock/framework/easybuild/framework/easyblock.py \
  --installed tests/sbom_recorded/easyblock/installed.txt \
  --reverse \
  --generated-at 2026-10-24T00:00:00Z \
  --out-dir /tmp/sbom-demo/ebreach/framework
```

```text
easyconfigs=4 installed=1 classes=5 reverse=0 out=/tmp/sbom-demo/ebreach/framework
```

```bash
sed -n '12,27p' /tmp/sbom-demo/ebreach/framework/reach.md
```

```text
Changed: ConfigureMake, EasyBlock, StopException.

Reached: CMakeMake, ConfigureMake, EB_GROMACS, EasyBlock, StopException.

## Easyconfigs

| Module | Class | Via | Detail | Installed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ADIOS2/2.10.2-foss-2025b` | `CMakeMake` | easyblock |  | no |
| `GROMACS/2024.4-foss-2024a` | `EB_GROMACS` | implied |  | no |
| `make/4.4.1-GCCcore-15.2.0` | `ConfigureMake` | easyblock |  | no |
| `zfp/1.0.1-GCCcore-15.2.0` | `CMakeMake` | easyblock |  | yes |

## Rebuild

None.
```

Changing `easybuild/framework/easyblock.py` reaches `EasyBlock`,
`StopException`, and the subclasses in the recorded easyblocks tree:
`ConfigureMake`, `CMakeMake`, and `EB_GROMACS`. `make` is now in the
table. `reverse=0` again, for the same reason as the CMakeMake run.

# The same document over MCP

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) catalog has 42 tools. `tools/list` prints
their names:

```bash
printf '%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}' \
  | eb-stack mcp \
  | jq -r '.result.tools[].name'
```

```text
eb_package_inspect
eb_package_plan
eb_package_bump
eb_recipe_read
eb_recipe_list
eb_recipe_edit
eb_recipe_apply_suggestion
eb_recipe_diff
eb_recipe_write
eb_recipe_grep
eb_recipe_easyblock
eb_recipe_templates
eb_recipe_hierarchy
eb_recipe_check
eb_recipe_lint
eb_dep_versions
eb_recipe_format
eb_module_lint
eb_easyblock_dry_run
eb_build_log
eb_build_test
eb_stack_solve
eb_stack_sbom
eb_stack_order
eb_stack_easystack
eb_package_latest
eb_stack_gap
eb_stack_batch
eb_stack_arch
eb_stack_sections
eb_stack_from_commit
eb_component_reach
eb_target_list
eb_target_doctor
eb_campaign_run
eb_campaign_status
eb_campaign_finding_claim
eb_campaign_finding_resolve
eb_pr_overlap
eb_rebuild_set
eb_easyblock_reach
eb_repro_summary
```

That is 42 tools. `eb_stack_sbom` writes the CycloneDX file `stack sbom`
writes. Its `tools/list` description reads: "Emit CycloneDX from an existing
stack lock, reading dependency edges and source checksums from the
easyconfigs the lock names." `eb_stack_sbom` reads the Cbc lock:

```bash
printf '%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"eb_stack_sbom","arguments":{"lock":"/tmp/sbom-demo/stack.lock.json","out":"/tmp/sbom-demo/mcp-stack.cdx.json"}}}' \
  | eb-stack mcp
```

```text
{"id":2,"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"content":[{"text":"{\n  \"components\": 58,\n  \"lock\": \"/tmp/sbom-demo/stack.lock.json\",\n  \"out\": \"/tmp/sbom-demo/mcp-stack.cdx.json\",\n  \"recipes_read\": 58,\n  \"recipes_unreadable\": 0,\n  \"with_artifact_facts\": 55\n}","type":"text"}],"isError":false,"structuredContent":{"components":58,"lock":"/tmp/sbom-demo/stack.lock.json","out":"/tmp/sbom-demo/mcp-stack.cdx.json","recipes_read":58,"recipes_unreadable":0,"with_artifact_facts":55}}}
```

```bash
jq -S 'del(.serialNumber)' /tmp/sbom-demo/mcp-stack.cdx.json > /tmp/sbom-demo/mcp.norm.json
cmp -s /tmp/sbom-demo/lock.norm.json /tmp/sbom-demo/mcp.norm.json && echo identical
```

```text
identical
```

The MCP document matches `stack sbom` once the serial number is removed.
`components` is 58 and `with_artifact_facts` is 55, the same counts as the
lock command above. The `dependsOn` edges are the edges that command wrote
for Cbc 2.10.12.

# Contributing

This page mirrors the repository `CONTRIBUTING.md` for the documentation
site. The source of truth for development gates is the markdown file at the
repo root; keep them aligned when you change either.

# Development environment

Rust 1.88 is the minimum supported toolchain; current stable runs the main test
and lint gates. Documentation uses [pixi](https://pixi.sh):

```bash
cargo test --locked --lib
cargo test --locked --test reproduce_real_prs --test bump_emit
pixi run -e docs docbld
```

# Code style and gates

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` when you touch Rust
- Tests relevant to your change must pass
- New public CLI surface needs a flag entry in [CLI reference](https://eb-stack.rgoswami.me/reference/cli.html.md)
  and a unit or integration test under `tests/`
- Known maintainer-bump regressions in `tests/reproduce_real_prs.rs` must
  stay green (library **and** CLI auto-bump)

# Documentation

Primary docs live in orgmode under `docs/orgmode/` (Diataxis). Edit there,
then build. The Sphinx site includes an in-tree Rust API (`crates/eb_stack/`)
via `sphinx-rustdocgen` + `sphinxcontrib_rust` (same path as rsx-rs).

```bash
# once: isolated system-Python environment for the native Rust extension
python3 -m venv .venv-docs
export RUSTFLAGS='-C linker=cc'
export CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_GNU_LINKER=cc
.venv-docs/bin/pip install 'sphinx>=9,<10' shibuya sphinx-sitemap \
  sphinx-copybutton sphinx-design 'sphinxcontrib-rust>=1,<2' \
  'sphinx-rustdoc-postprocess>=0.1,<0.2'
cargo install sphinx-rustdocgen

export EB_STACK_DOCS_PYTHON=$PWD/.venv-docs/bin/python
pixi run -e docs docbld
scripts/check-doc-links.sh docs/build
pixi run -e docs linkcheck
# HTML -> docs/build/index.html
```

The Sphinx task treats warnings as errors. The rendered-link check rejects
links to generated RST and incorrect source-edit targets; the Lychee task
checks the rendered site and README links.

`sphinxcontrib-rust` contains a native Rust extension. The explicit linker
environment keeps that extension on the host Rust/C linker rather than a
linker injected by the documentation package environment.

Do not hand-edit generated `docs/source/**/*.rst` or `docs/source/crates/`.

# Packaging campaigns

Follow the build, test, lint and docs commands at the repository root,
`skills/annual-bump/SKILL.md` (generation rebuild), and
`skills/new-package/SKILL.md` (conda-forge/Spack: new recipe). Run
`skills/verify-recipe/SKILL.md` over what they emit before a build or a push,
and `skills/tool-repair/SKILL.md` when the emitted file needed a hand
correction: a manual fix that does not return as a regression test is a
defect this tool reproduces on the next run. Keep site hostnames, paths,
credentials, scheduler sizing, and private module names in the site target
layer. Public files contain reusable package intent and target topology.

# Releasing

Version source of truth is `version` in root `Cargo.toml`. Keep these aligned:

1. `Cargo.toml` / `pixi.toml` `version`
2. `CITATION.cff` `version` and `date-released` for a published version
3. `docs/source/conf.py` `release`
4. `CHANGELOG.md` version heading and release date

Tag `vX.Y.Z` and push the tag. The release workflow builds the Linux archive
and checksum and publishes the GitHub Release.

# Changelog

The tagged release is 0.3.0. Cargo, CITATION, and Sphinx still report
**0.3.0**. Changes since that tag are the Unreleased section of
[CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/HaoZeke/eb-stack/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

The version-one design provides:

- one canonical package plan for conda-forge, Spack, and EasyBuild;
- planned CycloneDX plus per-profile Resolvo locks;
- one conventional EasyBuild recipe per installable profile;
- package-source catalogs, source-root discovery, and recursive closure;
- in-solver stack pin fallback and candidate exclusions;
- layered target routing and persisted typed build campaigns;
- independent resolves, builds, and binary-verified claims;
- matching CLI, Model Context Protocol (MCP), new-package skill, and
  annual-bump skill workflows, with recipe lint and the stack software
  bill of materials (SBOM) among the MCP tools;
- graph ordering, easystack emission, and Jenkins section regrouping;
- a reproduction scoreboard summary;
- easyblock dry-run, module lint, and build tools on the MCP server.

The scaffold/compatibility command surface is removed rather than maintained
alongside the canonical workflow.
